## 135. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Group.from_file.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.group.from_file}

# Group.from\_file[](#group-from-file "Link to this heading")

*classmethod* Group.from\_file(*src: str | os.PathLike[str] | BaseDataFile*, *loc: str = '/'*, *\**, *data: bool = True*, *format\_specific: FormatSpecificReadOptions | None = None*, *idxs: IdxsOption | None = None*, *idxs\_tol: float | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*, *src\_format: str | None = None*, *varnames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None*) → [Group](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Group.from_file "Link to this definition")
:   Read a datafile and return a new instance of Group.

    Known readable file extensions are stored in `options.reading.extensions`.
    Known readable file formats are stored in `options.reading.formats`.

    Parameters:
    :   * **src** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The source file path. If it has a missing or unknown file
          extension, you must either 1) input a [`DataFile`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile") with a
          `format_override`, or 2) use the `src_format` parameter.
        * **loc** (*str, default ‘/’*) – The location within the source file to return as a Group. If
          `'/'` (the “root”), the entire source file is read.
          Otherwise, it represents the name or position of a Group in
          the source file (for example, `'/0'` or `'/Group1`).
        * **data** (*bool, default True*) – A bool that determines whether to read the data from `src`. If
          `False`, only the metadata is read. Reading only metadata can
          be useful for quickly examining the variable names and hierarchy
          of `src`.
        * **format\_specific** (*FormatSpecificReadOptions, optional*) – Defines the format-specific options for reading `src`. By
          default, the global option
          `options.reading.format_specific` sets format-specific
          reading options, but this parameter can override the global
          options. If provided, it must be an instance of
          `FormatSpecificReadOptions`. See the docs for a list of
          all classes that can act as format-specific read options. Some
          examples are [`ADSReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions"),
          [`LoadPullReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions"), and [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars").
        * **idxs** (*{‘auto’, True, False}, optional*) – If `True`, create index variables (idxs) when reading the
          source file. If `False`, do not create them. If `'auto'`,
          use the format-specific defaults. If `None`, use the global
          option `options.reading.idxs`.
        * **idxs\_tol** (*float, optional*) – The tolerance to use when generating index variables from float
          or complex data. If NaN, no tolerance is used and indexes are
          created by using exact equality. If provided, it takes precedence
          over the global option `options.reading.idxs_tol`.
        * **iffs** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing.
        * **src\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the source file’s format. Supported types are stored in
          `options.reading.formats`. Any value other than `None`
          overrides the format inferred from or set by `src`.
        * **varnames** (*Mapping[str, str], optional*) – A mapping of variable roles to variable names. Defaults to
          `options.reading.varnames`.

    Return type:
    :   [*Group*](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group")

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following imports:

    ```
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    ```

    If the source file `src` has a known file extension, and you want
    to read the entire file, you can simply input `src` as a str,
    `pathlib.Path`, or `DataFile`.
    Known file extensions are stored in
    `pwdatatools.options.reading.extensions`.

    ```
    >>> # Using a str path with known ext (.ds)
    >>> g1 = pwdt.Group.from_file('/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> # Using pathlib.Path with known ext (.mdf)
    >>> g2 = pwdt.Group.from_file(Path('/home/noise_param.mdf'))
    >>> # Using DataFile with a known ext (.mdm)
    >>> g3 = pwdt.Group.from_file(pwdt.DataFile('/home/FNoise.mdm'))
    ```

    If `src` has a missing or unknown file extension, you can use the
    `src_format` parameter. Alternatively, you can input an instance of
    `DataFile` as the `src`
    argument and use DataFile’s `format_override` parameter to define
    the source’s format.

    ```
    >>> # Using the `src_format` parameter since the file extension is missing
    >>> g1 = pwdt.Group.from_file('/data/noise', src_format='mdif')
    >>> # Using the `src_format` parameter since the file extension is non-standard
    >>> g2 = pwdt.Group.from_file('/data/noise.txt', src_format='mdif')
    >>> # Using DataFile's `format_override` parameter is another option
    >>> datafile = pwdt.DataFile('/data/noise', format_override='mdif')
    >>> g3 = pwdt.Group.from_file(datafile)
    ```

    If you want to perform a partial read, use the `loc` parameter. You
    have to know the name of the part that you want to read from `src`.
    A Group will always be returned, even if the contents could be
    contained within a single Block (the Block is placed into a Group and
    the Group is returned).

    ```
    >>> # partial read of ADS dataset returns Group containing one Block
    >>> group1 = pwdt.Group.from_file('/home/s_param.ds', loc='/SP1.SP')
    >>> # partial read of a .pwdt file
    >>> group2 = pwdt.Group.from_file('/home/ac_dc_meas.pwdt', loc='/DUT5')
    ```

    See also

    `read_file()`
    `Block.from_file()`


---

## 136. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Group.get_member.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.group.get_member}

# Group.get\_member[](#group-get-member "Link to this heading")

Group.get\_member(*loc\_or\_index: str | int*) → Member[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Group.get_member "Link to this definition")
:   Get a member by string location or integer index.

    Parameters:
    :   **loc** (*str or int*) – The location or integer index of the member to get.

    Returns:
    :   The member at the given location or index.

    Return type:
    :   Member

    Raises:
    :   **ValueError** – If the location or index is invalid.

    Examples

    Let’s create a Group with two Blocks and get a member by location.

    ```
    >>> b0 = Block(name="b0")
    >>> b1 = Block(name="b1")
    >>> g = Group([b1, b2])
    >>> g.get_member("0").name
    'b0'
    ```

    It’s equivalent if we use a leading forward slash.

    ```
    >>> g.get_member("/0").name
    'b0'
    ```

    In this case, it’s also equivalent to use the Block’s name.
    However, be cautious when using names because it returns
    the first member with a matching name.

    ```
    >>> g.get_member("b0").name
    'b0'
    ```

    Let’s get a member by integer index instead.

    ```
    >>> g.get_member(1).name
    'b1'
    ```

    Now, let’s examine nested Groups.

    ```
    >>> b0 = Block(name="b0")
    >>> b1 = Block(name="b1")
    >>> g0 = Group([b0, b1], name="g0")
    >>> b2 = Block(name="b2")
    >>> b3 = Block(name="b3")
    >>> g1 = Group([b2, b3], name="g1")
    >>> g = Group([g0, g1], name="g")
    >>> g.get_member("0/0").name
    'b0'
    >>> g.get_member("1/1").name
    'b3'
    ```

    We can also use the names of the Groups and Blocks.

    ```
    >>> g.get_member("g0/b0").name
    'b0'
    >>> g.get_member("g1/b3").name
    'b3'
    ```

    We can even mix and match names and indices.

    ```
    >>> g.get_member("g0/1").name
    'b1'
    >>> g.get_member("1/b2").name
    'b2'
    ```

    If the loc is a lone forward slash, it returns the Group itself.

    ```
    >>> g.get_member("/").name
    'g'
    ```

## 137. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Group.get_member_as_block.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.group.get_member_as_block}

    can retrieve a Block inside of a child Group (if using string loc).

        a Block.

    Returns:
    :   The member as a Block.

    Return type:
    :   [*Block*](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")

    Raises:
    :   **ValueError** –

        * If loc or index is not found in the Group.
          - If loc or index corresponds to a Group instead of a Block.

## 139. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Group.get_member_as_loadpullblock.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.group.get_member_as_loadpullblock}

# Group.get\_member\_as\_loadpullblock[](#group-get-member-as-loadpullblock "Link to this heading")

Group.get\_member\_as\_loadpullblock(*loc\_or\_index: str | int*) → [LoadPullBlock](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools._api.loadpull.main.LoadPullBlock")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Group.get_member_as_loadpullblock "Link to this definition")
:   Return a member as a LoadPullBlock, retrieving it by string location or integer index.

    This method is preferred over `__getitem__` because it is more
    explicit in its return type. It is also more flexible because it
    can retrieve a LoadPullBlock inside of a child Group (if using string loc).

    Note that this method cannot cast a Block as a LoadPullBlock, because
    that operation would involve copying data (and violate expectations
    of “getting” a member). Instead, use [`LoadPullBlock.from_block()`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_block "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_block")
    to create a LoadPullBlock from a Block.

    Parameters:
    :   **loc\_or\_index** (*str or int*) – The string loc or integer index of the member to retrieve as
        a LoadPullBlock.

    Returns:
    :   The member as a LoadPullBlock.

    Return type:
    :   [*LoadPullBlock*](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")

    Raises:
    :   **ValueError** –

        * If loc or index is not found in the Group.
          - If loc or index corresponds to a Block or Group instead of a
          LoadPullBlock.

    See also

    [`LoadPullBlock.from_block()`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_block "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_block")

## 143. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Group.iter_members.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.group.iter_members}

# Group.iter\_members[](#group-iter-members "Link to this heading")

Group.iter\_members(*\**, *recursive: bool = False*) → Iterator[Member][](#keysight.pwdatatools.Group.iter_members "Link to this definition")
:   Iterate over the members.

    Unlike the `__iter__()` method, this method can optionally
    iterate recursively over all members (including members inside
    child Groups).

    Parameters:
    :   **recursive** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, iterate recursively over all members (including
        members inside child Groups). If `False`, do not iterate
        over the members inside child Groups.

    Notes

    Each iteration yields a child Group or Block. If
    `recursive=True` and a child Group exists, the child Group is
    yielded, then its members are yielded one at a time. If a child
    Group has a child Group, that child Group is yielded, then its
    members are yielded one at a time, and so on.

    Return type:
    :   *Iterator*[Member]


---

## 147. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Group.to_file.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.group.to_file}

# Group.to\_file[](#group-to-file "Link to this heading")

Group.to\_file(*dst: str | PathLike[str] | BaseDataFile*, *dst\_mode: Literal['x', 'w', 'a'] = 'x'*, *\**, *dst\_format: str | None = None*, *format\_specific: FormatSpecificWriteOptions | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*, *loc: str = '/'*) → None[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Group.to_file "Link to this definition")
:   Write Group to a file.

    If the destination file has a missing or unknown file extension,
    you must either 1) input a [`DataFile`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile") with a
    `format_override` as `dst`, or 2) use the `dst_format`
    parameter. Known writeable file extensions are stored in
    `options.writing.extensions`. Known writeable file formats
    are stored in `options.writing.formats`.

    Whether metadata is written depends on the format of output file.
    If the output file’s format has places to store metadata (e.g.
    such as in the native pwdatatools format or HDF5 format), then
    metadata is automatically included in the output file.

    Parameters:
    :   * **dst** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The destination file path.
        * **dst\_mode** (*{‘x’, ‘w’, ‘a’}, default ‘x’*) – The mode to use when opening `dst`. If `dst` does not yet
          exist, all three modes yield the same behavior. However, the 3
          modes have differing behaviors if attempting to write to a pre-
          existing file. `'w'` overwrites the existing file. `'a'`
          appends to the existing file. `'x'` results in a
          FileExistsError.
        * **dst\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the destination file’s format. Supported types are stored
          in `options.writing.formats`. Any value other than
          `None` overrides the format inferred from or set by `dst`.
        * **format\_specific** (*FormatSpecificWriteOptions, optional*) – Defines the format-specific options for writing `dst`. By
          default, the global option
          `options.writing.format_specific` sets format-specific
          writing options, but this parameter overrides the global
          options. If provided, it must be an instance of
          `FormatSpecificWriteOptions`. See the docs for a list
          of all classes that are format-specific write options. Some
          examples are `ADSWriteOptions`,
          `MDIFWriteOptions`, [`ADSWriteInvalid`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid"), and
          [`MDIFWriteInvalid`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid").
        * **iffs** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing.
        * **loc** (*str, default ‘/’*) – The write location within `dst`. Only applies to file
          formats that support multiple levels of hierarchy (for
          example, native and HDF5 formats). This parameter sets the
          write location within the file’s directory-like (or tree-like)
          structure. The “root” location is ‘/’.

    Return type:
    :   *None*

    Raises:
    :   * **FileExistsError** – If `dst_mode='x'` and `dst` already exists.
        * **ValueError** – If `dst_mode='a'` and append mode is not supported for the
          format of `dst`.

    Examples

    The below examples assume that `group` is an instance of
    [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools._api.group.Group") and the following
    imports:

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import DataFile
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    ```

    If the destination file `dst` has a known file extension, you can
    simply input `dst` as a str, `pathlib.Path`, or
    `DataFile`. Known file
    extensions are stored in `options.writing.extensions`.

    ```
    >>> # str path with known ext (.ds)
    >>> group.to_file('/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> # Path with known ext (.mdf)
    >>> group.to_file(Path('/home/noise_param.mdf'))
    >>>  # DataFile with known ext
    >>> group.to_file(DataFile('/home/noise_param.pwdt'))
    ```

    If the destination file `dst` has a missing or non-standard file
    extension, you can use the `dst_format` parameter. Alternatively,
    you can input an instance of
    `DataFile` as the `dst`
    argument and use the DataFile’s `format_override` parameter to
    define the destination’s format.

    ```
    >>> # no ext solved by dst_format
    >>> group.to_file('/data/s_param', dst_format='mdif')
    >>> # non-standard ext solved by dst_format
    >>> group.to_file('/data/noise_param.txt', dst_format='mdif')
    >>> # no ext solved by DataFile
    >>> group.to_file(DataFile('/data/noise_param', format_override='mdif'))
    ```

    If the destination file `dst` already exists, a FileExistsError is
    raised if `dst_mode='x'`, which is the default. A `dst_mode`
    parameter value of `'w'` will overwrite the entire existing file,
    while a value of `'a'` will append to the existing file.

    Note

    Only certain types of datafiles work for `dst_mode='a'`. A
    ValueError is raised if append mode is not supported for the format
    of `dst`.

    ```
    >>> group.to_file('/sparam.ds', dst_mode='w')  # overwrite dst, if it exists
    >>> group.to_file('/sparam.mdf', dst_mode='a') # append to dst, if it exists
    >>> group.to_file('/run1.pwdt', dst_mode='a') # append to dst, if it exists
    ```

    See also

    `write_file()`


---

## 148. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Group.tree.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.group.tree}

# Group.tree[](#group-tree "Link to this heading")

Group.tree() → str[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Group.tree "Link to this definition")
:   Return a tree view of this Group, similar to a directory tree.

    In the tree, each sub-Group is represented as a “folder” and each
    Block is represented as a “file”. This Group is treated as the
    “root” directory.

    The tree is returned as a string with newlines separating each
    level of the tree. The tree is indented to show the hierarchy.
    The string is meant to be printed to the console or shown in a
    GUI, not for programmatic use.

    Returns:
    :   Representation of the Group as a tree.

    Return type:
    :   *str*

    Examples

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> group = pwdt.read_file_as_group('/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> print(group.tree())
    <[/] Group 's_param'>
    ├── <[0] Block 'Sweep1.SP1.SP' with 4 Vars and 6 observations>
    ├── <[1] Block 'aele_0.Sweep1.SP1' with 3 Vars and 6 observations>
    └── <[2] Block 'aele_1.Sweep1.SP1' with 2 Vars and 2 observations>
    ```


---

## 149. api_reference\metadata.md {#api_reference--metadata}

# Metadata[](#metadata "Link to this heading")

This section contains documentation for the classes that store metadata for Vars, Blocks, and Groups.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [`AttrsDict`](_autosummary/keysight.pwdatatools.AttrsDict.md#keysight.pwdatatools.AttrsDict "keysight.pwdatatools.AttrsDict") | A type-restricted dict that stores arbitrary attributes (metadata) for [`Var`](_autosummary/keysight.pwdatatools.Var.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Var "keysight.pwdatatools.Var"), [`Block`](_autosummary/keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block"), and [`Group`](_autosummary/keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group"). |

:   A type-restricted dict that stores arbitrary attributes (metadata) for [`Var`](keysight.pwdatatools.Var.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Var "keysight.pwdatatools.Var"), [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block"), and [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group").

## 162. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.dims}

# Dims[](#dims "Link to this heading")

*class* Dims[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims "Link to this definition")
:   Dimensional metadata for a [`Var`](keysight.pwdatatools.Var.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Var "keysight.pwdatatools.Var").

    This class stores metadata for the “idx”, “i” and “j” dimensions,
    which correspond to the first, second, and third dimensions of a Var,
    respectively.

    This object is immutable. To modify a Var’s Dims, create a new Dims
    object with the desired changes and assign it to the Var’s dims property.
    For example, see the [`Dims.replace()`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.replace.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.replace "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.replace") method.

    Examples

    Let’s make a 1D Var with the default empty Dims.

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import Var
    >>> x = Var([10, 12, 13], name='x')
    >>> x.dims
    Dims(ndim=1)
    >>> x.has_dims()
    False
    ```

    Initializing a 2D Var or 3D Var without explicitly providing a
    dims argument also results in empty Dims, just like the 1D case.

    ```
    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> data_2d = np.random.random(6).reshape((3, 2))
    >>> var_2d = Var(data_2d, name='var_2d')
    >>> var_2d.dims
    Dims(ndim=2)
    >>> var_2d.has_dims()
    False
    >>> data_3d = np.random.random(20).reshape((5, 2, 2))
    >>> var_3d = Var(data_3d, name='var_3d')
    >>> var_3d.dims
    Dims(ndim=3)
    >>> var_3d.has_dims()
    False
    ```

    Now, let’s add an idx to the Dims of a 1D Var.

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import Dims
    >>> dims = Dims(ndim=1, idx=[1, 2, 3])
    >>> x = Var([10, 12, 13], name='x', dims=dims)
    >>> x.dims
    Dims(
        ndim=1,
        idx=[1, 2, 3],
    )
    ```

    Now, let’s initialize a 2D Var with dims that include i\_names,
    which enables indexing along the “i” dimension using strings
    instead of integers.

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import Dims
    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> dims = Dims(ndim=2, i_names=['P1', 'P2'])
    >>> var_2d_dims = Var(data_2d, name='var_2d_dims', dims=dims)
    >>> var_2d_dims.dims
    Dims(
        ndim=2,
        idx=None,
        i_nums=None,
        i_names=['P1', 'P2'],
    )
    ```

    Below, we initialize a 3D Var with dims that include i\_nums,
    which enables indexing along the “i” and “j” dimensions using
    arbitrary integers, rather than just 0-based or 1-based integers.

    ```
    >>> dims = Dims(ndim=3, i_nums=[3, 4], j_nums=[7, 8])
    >>> var_3d_dims = Var(data_3d, name='s', dims=dims)
    >>> var_3d_dims.dims
    Dims(
        ndim=3,
        idx=None,
        i_nums=[3, 4],
        i_names=None,
        j_nums=[7, 8],
        j_names=None,
    )
    ```

    See also

    [`Var.select()`](keysight.pwdatatools.Var.select.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Var.select "keysight.pwdatatools.Var.select")
    :   Index a Var using its Dims.

    [`Var.dims`](keysight.pwdatatools.Var.dims.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Var.dims "keysight.pwdatatools.Var.dims")
    :   Get or set the Dims for a Var

    [`Var.has_dims()`](keysight.pwdatatools.Var.has_dims.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Var.has_dims "keysight.pwdatatools.Var.has_dims")
    :   Return True if a Var has non-empty Dims.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`i_names`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.i_names.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.i_names "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.i_names") | Get i\_names as a string DimScale, or None if it is not set. |
    | [`i_nums`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.i_nums.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.i_nums "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.i_nums") | Get the i\_nums scale as an unsigned integer DimScale, or None if it is not set. |
    | [`idx`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.idx.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.idx "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.idx") | Get the idx scale as an unsigned integer DimScale, or None if it is not set. |
    | [`j_names`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.j_names.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.j_names "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.j_names") | Get the j\_names scale as a string DimScale, or None if it is not set. |
    | [`j_nums`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.j_nums.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.j_nums "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.j_nums") | Get the j\_nums scale as an unsigned integer DimScale, or None if it is not set. |
    | [`ndim`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.ndim.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.ndim "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.ndim") | Get the number of dimensions. |

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.__init__.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.__init__ "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.__init__")(\*, ndim[, idx, i\_nums, i\_names, ...]) | Initialize the Dims object. |
    | [`copy`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.copy.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.copy "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.copy")() | Create a copy of the Dims object. |
    | [`get_dimscale`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.get_dimscale.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.get_dimscale "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.get_dimscale")(dimscale\_name) | Get the DimScale for the specified dimension. |
    | [`has_i_names`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_i_names.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_i_names "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_i_names")() | Return True if an i\_names scale exists, else False. |
    | [`has_i_nums`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_i_nums.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_i_nums "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_i_nums")() | Return True if an i\_nums scale exists, else False. |
    | [`has_idx`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_idx.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_idx "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_idx")() | Return True if an idx scale exists, else False. |
    | [`has_j_names`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_j_names.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_j_names "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_j_names")() | Return True if a j\_names scale exists, else False. |
    | [`has_j_nums`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_j_nums.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_j_nums "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.has_j_nums")() | Return True if a j\_nums scale exists, else False. |
    | [`is_compatible_with_shape`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.is_compatible_with_shape.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.is_compatible_with_shape "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.is_compatible_with_shape")(shape) | Check if the Dims object is compatible with the given shape. |
    | [`is_empty`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.is_empty.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.is_empty "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.is_empty")() | Return True if none of the dimensions have scales, else False. |
    | [`keep_where`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.keep_where.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.keep_where "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.keep_where")(condition) | Create a new Dims object keeping scale values where the condition is True. |
    | [`partial_shape`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.partial_shape.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.partial_shape "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.partial_shape")() | Return shape of the Dims object, with any unknown dimension sizes equal to None. |
    | [`replace`](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.replace.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.replace "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.replace")(\*\*kwargs) | Create a new Dims object with the specified attribute(s) replaced. |

## 169. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.__init__.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.dims.__init__}

# Dims.\_\_init\_\_[](#dims-init "Link to this heading")

Dims.\_\_init\_\_(*\**, *ndim: int*, *idx: DimScaleLike | None = None*, *i\_nums: DimScaleLike | None = None*, *i\_names: DimScaleLike | None = None*, *j\_nums: DimScaleLike | None = None*, *j\_names: DimScaleLike | None = None*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.__init__ "Link to this definition")
:   Initialize the Dims object.

    Parameters:
    :   * **ndim** (*int*) – The number of dimensions.
        * **idx** (*unsigned integer array-like, optional*) – The scale along the first dimension (also known as axis 0 or the
          “shared” dimension).
        * **i\_nums** (*unsigned integer array-like, optional*) – The numeric scale for the second dimension (also known as the
          “i” dimension).
        * **i\_names** (*string array-like, optional*) – The string scale for the second dimension (also known as the
          “i” dimension).
        * **j\_nums** (*unsigned integer array-like, optional*) – The numeric scale for the third dimension (also known as the
          “j” dimension).
        * **j\_names** (*string array-like, optional*) – The string scale for the third dimension (also known as the
          “j” dimension).

    Examples

    Let’s make a 1D Var with the default empty Dims.

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import Var
    >>> x = Var([10, 12, 13], name='x')
    >>> x.dims
    Dims(ndim=1)
    >>> x.has_dims()
    True
    ```

    Initializing a 2D Var or 3D Var without explicitly providing a
    dims argument also results in empty Dims, just like the 1D case.

    ```
    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> data_2d = np.random.random(6).reshape((3, 2))
    >>> var_2d = Var(data_2d, name='var_2d')
    >>> var_2d.dims
    Dims(ndim=2)
    >>> var_2d.has_dims()
    True
    >>> data_3d = np.random.random(20).reshape((5, 2, 2))
    >>> var_3d = Var(data_3d, name='var_3d')
    >>> var_3d.dims
    Dims(ndim=3)
    >>> var_3d.has_dims()
    True
    ```

    Now, let’s add an idx to the Dims of a 1D Var.

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import Dims
    >>> dims = Dims(ndim=1, idx=[1, 2, 3])
    >>> x = Var([10, 12, 13], name='x', dims=dims)
    >>> x.dims
    Dims(
        ndim=1,
        idx=[1, 2, 3],
    )
    ```

    Now, let’s initialize a 2D Var with dims that include i\_names,
    which enables indexing along the “i” dimension using strings
    instead of integers.

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import Dims
    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> dims = Dims(ndim=2, i_names=['P1', 'P2'])
    >>> var_2d_dims = Var(data_2d, name='var_2d_dims', dims=dims)
    >>> var_2d_dims.dims
    Dims(
        ndim=2,
        idx=None,
        i_nums=None,
        i_names=['P1', 'P2'],
    )
    ```

    Below, we initialize a 3D Var with dims that include i\_nums,
    which enables indexing along the “i” and “j” dimensions using
    arbitrary integers, rather than just 0-based or 1-based integers.

    ```
    >>> dims = Dims(ndim=3, i_nums=[3, 4], j_nums=[7, 8])
    >>> var_3d_dims = Var(data_3d, name='s', dims=dims)
    >>> var_3d_dims.dims
    Dims(
        ndim=3,
        idx=None,
        i_nums=[3, 4],
        i_names=None,
        j_nums=[7, 8],
        j_names=None,
    )
    ```

# Dims.keep\_where[](#dims-keep-where "Link to this heading")

Dims.keep\_where(*condition: NDArray[np.bool\_]*) → [Dims](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.keep_where "Link to this definition")
:   Create a new Dims object keeping scale values where the condition is True.

    Along each dimension of the input condition, if any value is True, keep that
    scale value in the returned Dims. If all values are False, drop that scale value.

    Parameters:
    :   **condition** (*numpy.ndarray*) – A boolean array with a shape that is compatible with the Dims object.

    Returns:
    :   The new Dims object.

    Return type:
    :   [*Dims*](keysight.pwdatatools.Dims.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Dims "keysight.pwdatatools.Dims")

    immutable, meaning that once it is created, its values and name cannot be changed.

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.__init__.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.__init__ "keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.__init__")(values, /, \*[, name]) | Initialize an instance of DimScale. |
    | [`copy`](keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.copy.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.copy "keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.copy")() | Return a copy of this DimScale instance. |
    | [`from_pandas_index`](keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.from_pandas_index.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.from_pandas_index "keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.from_pandas_index")(index) | Return a DimScale instance from a pandas Index. |
    | [`has_names_values`](keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.has_names_values.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.has_names_values "keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.has_names_values")() | Return bool indicating whether the values are string. |
    | [`has_nums_values`](keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.has_nums_values.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.has_nums_values "keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.has_nums_values")() | Return bool indicating whether the values are numeric (unsigned integer). |
    | [`rename`](keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.rename.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.rename "keysight.pwdatatools.DimScale.rename")(name) | Return a new DimScale with the specified name. |

## 192. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.expr}

# Expr[](#expr "Link to this heading")

*class* Expr[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr "Link to this definition")
:   An object that represents an expression.

    This object stores an input and a list of operations to be performed
    on that input. Expressions are stored in [`Block.exprs`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.exprs.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block.exprs "keysight.pwdatatools.Block.exprs") attribute
    in an instance of [`ExprsDict`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict"). For more information and examples,
    see [Use the Block Class](../../howto/use_block_class.md#use-block-class).

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`input`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.input.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.input "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.input") | Return the input variable or expression. |
    | [`ops`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.ops.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.ops "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.ops") | Return the operations. |

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.__init__.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.__init__ "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.__init__")(input[, ops]) | Initialize instance of Expr. |
    | [`abs`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.abs.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.abs "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.abs")() | Return an expression that represents the absolute value of the expression. |
    | [`angle`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.angle.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.angle "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.angle")(\*[, deg]) | Return an expression that represents the angle of the expression. |
    | [`copy`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.copy.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.copy "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.copy")() | Return a deep copy of the Expr. |
    | [`dB`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.dB.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.dB "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.dB")(\*[, power]) | Return an expression that represents the decibel of the expression. |
    | [`decibel`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.decibel.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.decibel "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.decibel")(\*[, power]) | Return an expression that represents the decibel of the expression. |
    | [`eval_as_numpy_ndarray`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.eval_as_numpy_ndarray.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.eval_as_numpy_ndarray "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.eval_as_numpy_ndarray")([block]) | Return the result of the expression as a NumPy ndarray. |
    | [`imag`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.imag.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.imag "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.imag")() | Return an expression that represents the imaginary part of the expression. |
    | [`mag`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.mag.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.mag "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.mag")() | Return an expression that represents the magnitude of the expression. |
    | [`real`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.real.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.real "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.real")() | Return an expression that represents the real part of the expression. |


---

## 195. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.__init__.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.expr.__init__}

# Expr.\_\_init\_\_[](#expr-init "Link to this heading")

Expr.\_\_init\_\_(*input: InputLike*, *ops: OpsSequence | None = None*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.__init__ "Link to this definition")
:   Initialize instance of Expr.

    Parameters:
    :   * **input** (*array-like, scalar, or Expr*) – If a str, it is interpreted as a name of a variable or expression.
          Otherwise, it is interpreted as an array-like or scalar value.
        * **ops** (*sequence of Operation, optional*) – The operations to apply to the input.

    Notes

    The input and operations are stored as attributes of the Expr. If the input
    is a str, it is stored as a string. If the input is an array-like or scalar
    value, it is stored as a NumPy ndarray. The operations are stored as a tuple
    of Operation objects.


---

## 205. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.exprsdict}

# ExprsDict[](#exprsdict "Link to this heading")

*class* ExprsDict[](#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict "Link to this definition")
:   A mapping of string names (keys) to [`Expr`](keysight.pwdatatools.Expr.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Expr "keysight.pwdatatools.Expr") objects (values).

    This object stores expressions for [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block"), stored in the [`Block.exprs`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.exprs.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block.exprs "keysight.pwdatatools.Block.exprs") attribute.
    For more information and examples, see [Use the Block Class](../../howto/use_block_class.md#use-block-class). It behaves like a
    type-restricted dict.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`block`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.block "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.block") | Return the block. |

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.__init__.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.__init__ "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.__init__")([mapping]) | Initialize instance of ExprsDict. |
    | [`clear`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.clear.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.clear "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.clear")() |  |
    | [`copy`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.copy.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.copy "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.copy")() | Return a deep copy of the ExprsDict. |
    | [`get`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.get.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.get "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.get")(k[,d]) |  |
    | [`items`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.items.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.items "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.items")() |  |
    | [`keys`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.keys.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.keys "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.keys")() |  |
    | [`pop`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.pop.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.pop "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.pop")(k[,d]) | If key is not found, d is returned if given, otherwise KeyError is raised. |
    | [`popitem`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.popitem.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.popitem "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.popitem")() | as a 2-tuple; but raise KeyError if D is empty. |
    | [`setdefault`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.setdefault.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.setdefault "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.setdefault")(k[,d]) |  |
    | [`update`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.update.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.update "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.update")([E, ]\*\*F) | If E present and has a .keys() method, does: for k in E.keys(): D[k] = E[k] If E present and lacks .keys() method, does: for (k, v) in E: D[k] = v In either case, this is followed by: for k, v in F.items(): D[k] = v |
    | [`values`](keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.values.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.values "keysight.pwdatatools.ExprsDict.values")() |  |

## 219. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_block.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_block}

# read\_file\_as\_block[](#read-file-as-block "Link to this heading")

read\_file\_as\_block(*src: StrPathLike | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile")*, *loc: str = '/'*, *\**, *data: bool = True*, *format\_specific: FormatSpecificReadOptions | None = None*, *idxs: IdxsOption | None = None*, *idxs\_tol: float | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*, *src\_format: str | None = None*, *varnames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None*) → [Block](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_block "Link to this definition")
:   Read a datafile and return a new instance of Block.

    Known readable file extensions are stored in `options.reading.extensions`.
    Known readable file formats are stored in `options.reading.formats`.

    Parameters:
    :   * **src** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The source file path.
        * **loc,** (*str, default ‘/’*) – The location within the source file to return as a Block. If
          `'/'` (the “root”), the entire source file is read.
          Otherwise, it represents some portion of the source file. This
          may be the name of a single Block (for example, in an MDIF or
          ADS dataset), or the full path to a Group or Block (e.g.
          `'/G1/X'`, where ‘G1’ is the name of a Group and ‘X’ is the
          name of the desired Block).
        * **data** (*bool, default True*) – A bool that determines whether to read the data from `src`.
          If `False`, only the metadata is read. Reading only metadata
          can be useful for quickly examining information about the
          variables.
        * **format\_specific** (*FormatSpecificReadOptions, optional*) – Defines the format-specific options for reading `src`. By
          default, the global option
          `options.reading.format_specific` sets format-specific
          reading options, but this parameter can override the global
          options. If provided, it must be an instance of
          `FormatSpecificReadOptions`. See the docs for a list of
          all classes that can act as format-specific read options. Some
          examples are [`ADSReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions"),
          [`LoadPullReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions"), and [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars").
        * **idxs** (*{‘auto’, True, False}, optional*) – If `True`, create index variables (idxs) when reading the
          source file. If `False`, do not create them. If `'auto'`,
          use the format-specific defaults. If `None`, use the global
          option `options.reading.idxs`.
        * **idxs\_tol** (*float, optional*) – The tolerance to use when generating index variables from float
          or complex data. If NaN, no tolerance is used and indexes are
          created by using exact equality. If provided, it takes precedence
          over the global option `options.reading.idxs_tol`.
        * **iffs** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing.
        * **src\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the source file’s format. Supported types are stored in
          `options.reading.formats`. Any value other
          than `None` overrides the format inferred from or set by
          `src`.
        * **varnames** (*Mapping[str, str], optional*) – A mapping of variable roles to their names. Defaults to
          `options.reading.varnames`.

    Return type:
    :   [*Block*](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")

    Raises:
    :   **ValueError** – If data cannot be represented as a single Block.

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following imports:

    ```
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    ```

    If the source file `src` has a known file extension, and you want
    to read the entire file, you can simply input `src` as a str,
    `pathlib.Path`, or `DataFile`.
    Known file extensions are stored in `options.reading.extensions`.

    ```
    >>> # Using a str path with known ext (.lpd)
    >>> b1 = pwdt.read_file_as_block('/home/device.lpd')
    >>> # Using a pathlib.Path with known ext (.spl)
    >>> b2 = pwdt.read_file_as_block(Path('/home/device.spl'))
    >>> # Using a DataFile with a known ext (.mdm)
    >>> b3 = pwdt.read_file_as_block(pwdt.DataFile('/home/FNoise.mdm'))
    ```

    If `src` has a missing or unknown file extension, you can use
    the `src_format` parameter. Alternatively, you can input an
    instance of `DataFile` as
    the `src` argument and use DataFile’s `format_override`
    parameter to define the source’s format.

    ```
    >>> # Using the ``src_format`` parameter since the file extension is missing
    >>> b1 = pwdt.read_file_as_block('/data/noise', src_format='mdif')
    >>> # Using the ``src_format`` parameter since the file extension is non-standard
    >>> b2 = pwdt.read_file_as_block('/data/noise.txt', src_format='mdif')
    >>> # Using a DataFile with ``format_override`` is another option
    >>> b3 = pwdt.read_file_as_block(pwdt.DataFile('/noise', format_override='mdif'))
    ```

    If you want to perform a partial read, use the `loc` parameter.
    You have to know the name of the part that you want to read from
    `src`. A Block is always returned. If the contents of the part
    cannot be represented by a single Block, a ValueError is raised.

    ```
    >>> b1 = pwdt.read_file_as_block('/home/s_param.ds', loc='/SP1.SP')
    >>> b2 = pwdt.read_file_as_block('/home/ac_dc_meas.pwdt', loc='/Network')
    ```

    See also

    `Block.from_file()`


---

## 220. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_group.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_group}

# read\_file\_as\_group[](#read-file-as-group "Link to this heading")

read\_file\_as\_group(*src: StrPathLike | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile")*, *loc: str = '/'*, *\**, *data: bool = True*, *format\_specific: FormatSpecificReadOptions | None = None*, *idxs: IdxsOption | None = None*, *idxs\_tol: float | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*, *src\_format: str | None = None*, *varnames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None*) → [Group](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_group "Link to this definition")
:   Read a datafile and return a new instance of Group.

    Known readable file extensions are stored in `options.reading.extensions`.
    Known readable file formats are stored in `options.reading.formats`.

    Parameters:
    :   * **src** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The source file path.
        * **loc** (*str, default ‘/’*) – The location within the source file to return as a Group. If
          `'/'` (the “root”), the entire source file is read.
          Otherwise, it represents some portion of the source file. This
          may be the full path to a Group or Block (e.g. `'/parent/X'`,
          where ‘parent’ is the name of the parent Group and ‘X’ is the
          name of the desired Group or Block). If the contents of `loc`
          can be represented by a single Block, the Block is placed into a
          Group and the Group is returned.
        * **data** (*bool, default True*) – A bool that determines whether to read the data from `src`.
          If `False`, only the metadata is read. Reading only metadata
          can be useful for quickly examining information about the
          variables.
        * **format\_specific** (*FormatSpecificReadOptions, optional*) – Defines the format-specific options for reading `src`. By
          default, the global option
          `options.reading.format_specific` sets format-specific
          reading options, but this parameter can override the global
          options. If provided, it must be an instance of
          `FormatSpecificReadOptions`. See the docs for a list of
          all classes that can act as format-specific read options. Some
          examples are [`ADSReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions"),
          [`LoadPullReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions"), and [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars").
        * **idxs** (*{‘auto’, True, False}, optional*) – If `True`, create index variables (idxs) when reading the
          source file. If `False`, do not create them. If `'auto'`,
          use the format-specific defaults. If `None`, use the global
          option `options.reading.idxs`.
        * **idxs\_tol** (*float, optional*) – The tolerance to use when generating index variables from float
          or complex data. If NaN, no tolerance is used and indexes are
          created by using exact equality. If provided, it takes precedence
          over the global option `options.reading.idxs_tol`.
        * **iffs** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing.
        * **src\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the source file’s format. Supported types are stored in
          `options.reading.formats`. Any value other
          than `None` overrides the format inferred from or set by
          `src`.
        * **varnames** (*Mapping[str, str], optional*) – A mapping of variable roles to their names. Defaults to
          `options.reading.varnames`.

    Return type:
    :   [*Group*](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group")

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following imports:

    ```
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    ```

    If the source file `src` has a known file extension, and you want
    to read the entire file, you can simply input `src` as a str,
    `pathlib.Path`, or `DataFile`.
    Known file extensions are stored in
    `pwdatatools.options.reading.extensions`.

    ```
    >>> # Using a str path with known ext (.ds)
    >>> g1 = pwdt.read_file_as_group('/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> # Using pathlib.Path with known ext (.mdf)
    >>> g2 = pwdt.read_file_as_group(Path('/home/noise_param.mdf'))
    >>> # Using DataFile with a known ext (.mdm)
    >>> g3 = pwdt.read_file_as_group(pwdt.DataFile('/home/FNoise.mdm'))
    ```

    If `src` has a missing or unknown file extension, you can use the
    `src_format` parameter. Alternatively, you can input an instance of
    `DataFile` as the `src`
    argument and use DataFile’s `format_override` parameter to define
    the source’s format.

    ```
    >>> # Using the `src_format` parameter since the file extension is missing
    >>> g1 = pwdt.read_file_as_group('/data/noise', src_format='mdif')
    >>> # Using the `src_format` parameter since the file extension is non-standard
    >>> g2 = pwdt.read_file_as_group('/data/noise.txt', src_format='mdif')
    >>> # Using DataFile's `format_override` parameter is another option
    >>> g3 = pwdt.read_file_as_group(
    ...     pwdt.DataFile('/noise.txt', format_override='mdif')
    ... )
    ```

    If you want to perform a partial read, use the `loc` parameter. You
    have to know the name of the part that you want to read from `src`.
    A Group will always be returned, even if the contents could be
    contained within a single Block (the Block is placed into a Group and
    the Group is returned).

    ```
    >>> # partial read of ADS dataset returns Group containing one Block
    >>> group1 = pwdt.read_file_as_group('/home/s_param.ds', loc='/SP1.SP')
    >>> # partial read of a .pwdt file
    >>> group2 = pwdt.read_file_as_group('/home/ac_dc_meas.pwdt', loc='/Network')
    ```

    See also

    `Group.from_file()`


---

## 221. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_loadpullblock.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_loadpullblock}

# read\_file\_as\_loadpullblock[](#read-file-as-loadpullblock "Link to this heading")

read\_file\_as\_loadpullblock(*src: StrPathLike | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile")*, *\**, *format\_specific: [LoadPullReadOptions](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions") | [LoadPullDerivedVars](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars") | None = None*, *varnames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None*) → [LoadPullBlock](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.read_file_as_loadpullblock "Link to this definition")
:   Read a load pull datafile and return a LoadPullBlock.

    The source file must have a known file extension that is associated
    with Keysight, Focus, or Maury load pull files. Known readable load
    pull file extensions are stored in
    `options.reading.format_to_extension_map['loadpull']`.

    Parameters:
    :   * **src** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The source file path.
        * **format\_specific** (*FormatSpecificReadOptions, optional*) – Defines the format-specific options for reading `src`. By
          default, the global option
          `options.reading.format_specific` sets format-specific
          reading options, but this parameter can override the global
          options. If provided, it must be an instance of
          `FormatSpecificReadOptions`. See the docs for a list of
          all classes that can act as format-specific read options. Some
          examples are [`LoadPullReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions") and
          [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars").
        * **varnames** (*mapping of str to str, optional*) – A mapping of variable roles to their names. Defaults to
          `options.reading.varnames`.

    Return type:
    :   [*LoadPullBlock*](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")

    Examples

    Using all the default options:
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.read\_file\_as\_loadpullblock(“/data/loadpull.cst”)

    Modifying global options to control how variables are named and
    which variables are derived from a and b waves:

    ```
    >>> pwdt.options.reading.varnames["power.delivered.load"] = "Pout"
    >>> pwdt.options.reading.format_specific.loadpull.derived_vars.ampm = False
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.read_file_as_loadpullblock("/data/loadpull.cst")
    ```

    Passing in a dict of roles to varnames and an instance of
    [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars") to override the global settings:

    ```
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.read_file_as_loadpullblock(
    ...     "/data/loadpull.cst",
    ...     varnames={'gamma.load': 'GL'},
    ...     format_specific=pwdt.LoadPullDerivedVars(ampm=False),
    ... )
    ```

    See also

    `LoadPullBlock.from_file()`


---

## 222. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.read_file.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.read_file}

# read\_file[](#read-file "Link to this heading")

read\_file(*src: StrPathLike | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile")*, *loc: Literal['/'] = '/'*, *\**, *data: bool = True*, *format\_specific: FormatSpecificReadOptions | None = None*, *idxs: IdxsOption | None = None*, *idxs\_tol: float | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*, *src\_format: str | None = None*, *varnames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None*) → [Group](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools._api.group.Group")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.read_file "Link to this definition")

read\_file(*src: StrPathLike | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile")*, *loc: str*, *\**, *data: bool = True*, *format\_specific: FormatSpecificReadOptions | None = None*, *idxs: IdxsOption | None = None*, *idxs\_tol: float | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*, *src\_format: str | None = None*, *varnames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None*) → [Group](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools._api.group.Group") | [Block](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools._api.block.Block")
:   Read a datafile and return a Group or Block.

    Known readable file extensions are stored in `options.reading.extensions`.
    Known readable file formats are stored in `options.reading.formats`.

    Parameters:
    :   * **src** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The source file path.
        * **loc** (*str, default ‘/’*) – The location within the source file to return as a Group or Block.
          If `'/'` (the “root”), the entire source file is read and
          returned as a Group. Otherwise, it represents some portion of the
          source file. This may be the name of a single Block (for example,
          in an MDIF or ADS dataset), or the full path to a Group or Block
          (e.g. `'/G1/X'`, where ‘G1’ is the name of a Group and ‘X’ is
          the name of the desired Group or Block).
        * **data** (*bool, default True*) – A bool that determines whether to read the data from `src`.
          If `False`, only the metadata is read. Reading only metadata
          can be useful for quickly examining information about the
          variables.
        * **format\_specific** (*FormatSpecificReadOptions, optional*) – Defines the format-specific options for reading `src`. By
          default, the global option
          `options.reading.format_specific` sets format-specific
          reading options, but this parameter can override the global
          options. If provided, it must be an instance of
          `FormatSpecificReadOptions`. See the docs for a list of
          all classes that can act as format-specific read options. Some
          examples are [`ADSReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions"),
          [`LoadPullReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions"), and [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars").
        * **idxs** (*{‘auto’, True, False}, optional*) – If `True`, create index variables (idxs) when reading the
          source file. If `False`, do not create them. If `'auto'`,
          use the format-specific defaults. If `None`, use the global
          option `options.reading.idxs`.
        * **idxs\_tol** (*float, optional*) – The tolerance to use when generating index variables from float
          or complex data. If NaN, no tolerance is used and indexes are
          created by using exact equality. If provided, it takes precedence
          over the global option `options.reading.idxs_tol`.
        * **iffs** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing.
        * **src\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the source file’s format. Supported types are stored in
          `options.reading.formats`. Any value other
          than `None` overrides the format inferred from or set by
          `src`.
        * **varnames** (*Mapping[str, str], optional*) – A mapping of variable roles to their names. Defaults to
          `options.reading.varnames`.

    Returns:
    :   A [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group") or [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block") containing the contents of
        `src`. If `loc` is `'/'`, a [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group") is always
        returned. Otherwise, a [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block") is returned if the contents
        of `loc` can be represented by a single [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block"). If the
        contents of `loc` cannot be represented by a single
        [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block"), a [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group") is returned.

    Return type:
    :   *Union*[[*Group*](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group"), [*Block*](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")]

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following imports:

    ```
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    ```

    If the source file `src` has a known file extension, and you want
    to read the entire file, you can simply input `src` as a str,
    `pathlib.Path`, or `DataFile`.
    Known file extensions are stored in
    `pwdatatools.options.reading.extensions`.

    ```
    >>> # Using a str path with known ext (.ds)
    >>> g1 = pwdt.read_file('/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> # Using a pathlib.Path with known ext (.mdf)
    >>> g2 = pwdt.read_file(Path('/home/noise_param.mdf'))
    >>> # Using a DataFile with known ext (.mdm)
    >>> b3 = pwdt.read_file(pwdt.DataFile('/home/FNoise.mdm'))
    ```

    If `src` has a missing or unknown file extension, you can use the
    `src_format` parameter. Alternatively, you can input an instance of
    `DataFile` as the `src`
    argument and use DataFile’s `format_override` parameter to define
    the source’s format.

    ```
    >>> # Using src_format parameter since src has missing ext
    >>> g1 = pwdt.read_file('/data/noise', src_format='mdif')
    >>> # Using src_format parameter since src has non-standard ext
    >>> g2 = pwdt.read_file('/data/noise.txt', src_format='mdif')
    >>> # Using DataFile with format_override
    >>> b1 = pwdt.read_file(pwdt.DataFile('/data/noise.txt', format_override='mdif'))
    ```

    If you want to perform a partial read, use the `loc` parameter. You
    have to know the name of the part that you want to read from `src`.
    A Group or Block may be returned, depending on the contents of the
    part.

    ```
    >>> # partial read of ADS datasets always returns a Block
    >>> block1 = pwdt.read_file('/home/s_param.ds', loc='/SP1.SP')
    >>> # partial read of a .pwdt file may return Group or Block
    >>> group1 = pwdt.read_file('/home/ac_dc_meas.pwdt', loc='/Network')
    ```

    See also

    [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools._api.group.Group"), [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools._api.block.Block")

## 223. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.translate_file.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.translate_file}

# translate\_file[](#translate-file "Link to this heading")

translate\_file(*src: StrPathLike | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile")*, *dst: StrPathLike | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile")*, *dst\_mode: Literal['x', 'w', 'a'] = 'x'*, *\*\*kwargs*) → None[](#keysight.pwdatatools.translate_file "Link to this definition")
:   Translate a datafile from one format to another.

    There are several supported source and destination formats. The
    formats can be set explicitly using optional keyword parameters
    `src_format` and `dst_format`. However, if `src` and `dst` have
    recognized file extensions, the formats can be automatically
    inferred and the keyword arguments do not need to be used.

    Parameters:
    :   * **src** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The source file path. If `src_format=None`, attempts are
          made to ascertain the format by examining the source file’s
          extension. Known file extensions are stored in
          `options.reading.extensions`.
        * **dst** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The destination file path. If `dst_format=None`, attempts are
          made to ascertain the format by examining the destination file’s
          extension. Known file extensions are stored in
          `options.writing.extensions`.
        * **dst\_mode** (*{‘x’, ‘w’, ‘a’}, default ‘x’*) – The mode to use when opening `dst`. If `dst` does not yet
          exist, all three modes yield the same behavior. However, the 3
          modes have differing behaviors if attempting to write to a pre-
          existing file. `'w'` overwrites the existing file. `'a'`
          appends to the existing file. `'x'` results in a
          FileExistsError.

    Other Parameters:
    :   * **src\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the source file’s format. Supported types are stored in
          `options.reading.formats`. Any value other than `None`
          overrides the format inferred from or set by `src`.
        * **dst\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the destination file’s format. Supported types are stored in
          `options.writing.formats`. Any value other than
          `None` overrides the format inferred from or set by `dst`.
        * **iffs** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing.

    Return type:
    :   *None*

    Notes

    This function always uses the global format-specific read and write
    options. The only way to override the global options is to perform
    translation as a two-step process (read then write).

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following imports:

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import translate_file, DataFile
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    ```

    If the source file `src` and destination file `dst` both have
    known file extensions, simply input `src` and `dst` and nothing
    else.

    ```
    >>> # str src & dst with known exts (.s4p and .ds)
    >>> translate_file('/home/s_param.s4p', '/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> # pathlib.Path src & dst with known exts (.ds and .mdf)
    >>> translate_file(Path('/home/noise.ds'), Path('/home/noise.mdf'))
    >>> # str src & DataFile dst with known exts (.ds and .pwdt)
    >>> translate_file('/home/noise.ds', DataFile('/home/noise.pwdt'))
    ```

    If the the source file and/or destination file have missing or unknown
    file extensions, use the `src_format` and/or `dst_format` parameters.
    Alternatively, input an instance of
    `DataFile` as the `src` and/or
    `dst` arguments and use DataFile’s `format_override` parameter
    to define the format(s).

    ```
    >>> translate_file('/home/s_param', '/home/s_param.ds', src_format='touchstone')
    >>> translate_file('/noise', '/noise_new', src_format='ads', dst_format='mdif')
    >>> # Or, use DataFiles:
    >>> src = DataFile('/home/noise', format_override='mdif')
    >>> dst = DataFile('/home/noise_translated', format_override='pwdt')
    >>> translate_file(src, dst)
    ```

    If the destination file `dst` already exists, a FileExistsError is
    raised if `dst_mode='x'`, which is the default. A `dst_mode`
    parameter value of `'w'` will overwrite the entire existing file,
    while a value of `'a'` will append to the existing file.

    Note

    Only certain types of datafiles work for `dst_mode='a'`. A
    ValueError is raised if append mode is not supported for the format
    of `dst`.

    ```
    >>> # overwrite dst, if it exists
    >>> translate_file('/home/s_param.mdf', '/home/s_param.ds', dst_mode='w')
    >>> # append to dst, if it exists
    >>> translate_file('/home/s_param.ds', '/home/s_param.mdf', dst_mode='a')
    >>> # append to dst, if it exists
    >>> translate_file('/home/s_param.ds', '/home/s_param.pwdt', dst_mode='a')
    ```

    See also

    `DataFile.translate()`
    `read_file()`
    `write_file()`


---

## 224. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.write_file.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.write_file}

# write\_file[](#write-file "Link to this heading")

write\_file(*group\_or\_block: [Group](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group") | [Block](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")*, *dst: StrPathLike | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile")*, *dst\_mode: Literal['x', 'w', 'a'] = 'x'*, *\**, *dst\_format: str | None = None*, *\*\*kwargs*) → None[](#keysight.pwdatatools.write_file "Link to this definition")
:   Write a Group or Block to a file.

    Known writeable file extensions are stored in `options.writing.extensions`.
    Known writeable file formats are stored in `options.writing.formats`.

    Whether metadata is written depends on the format of output file.
    If the output file’s format has places to store metadata (such as
    in the native pwdatatools .pwdt format or HDF5 format), then metadata
    is automatically included in the output file.

    Parameters:
    :   * **group\_or\_block** (*Group or Block*) – An instance of [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group") or [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block") to write to a
          file.
        * **dst** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The destination file path. If it has a missing or unknown file
          extension, you must either 1) input a [`DataFile`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile") with a
          `format_override`, or 2) use the `dst_format` parameter.
        * **dst\_mode** (*{‘x’, ‘w’, ‘a’}, default ‘x’*) – The mode to use when opening `dst`. If `dst` does not yet
          exist, all three modes yield the same behavior. However, the 3
          modes have differing behaviors if attempting to write to a pre-
          existing file. `'w'` overwrites the existing file. `'a'`
          appends to the existing file. `'x'` results in a
          FileExistsError.
        * **dst\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the destination file’s format. Supported types are stored in
          `options.writing.formats`. Any value other than
          `None` overrides the format inferred from or set by `dst`.

    Other Parameters:
    :   * **format\_specific** (*FormatSpecificWriteOptions, optional*) – Defines the format-specific options for writing `dst`. By
          default, the global option
          `options.writing.format_specific` sets format-specific
          writing options, but this parameter overrides the global
          options. If provided, it must be an instance of
          `FormatSpecificWriteOptions`. See the docs for a list
          of all classes that are format-specific write options. Some
          examples are `ADSWriteOptions`,
          `MDIFWriteOptions`, [`ADSWriteInvalid`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid"), and
          [`MDIFWriteInvalid`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid").
        * **loc** (*str, default ‘/’*) – The write location within `dst`. Only applies to file
          formats that support multiple levels of hierarchy (for
          example, native and HDF5 formats). This parameter sets the
          write location within the file’s directory-like (or tree-like)
          structure. The “root” location is ‘/’.
        * **iffs** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing.

    Return type:
    :   *None*

    Examples

    The below examples assume that `group` is an instance of
    [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools._api.group.Group"), `block` is an
    instance of [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools._api.block.Block"), and
    the following imports:

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import write_file, DataFile
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    ```

    If the destination file `dst` has a known file extension, you can
    simply input `dst` as a str, `pathlib.Path`, or
    `DataFile`. Known file
    extensions are stored in `options.writing.extensions`.

    ```
    >>> # str path with a known ext (.ds)
    >>> write_file(group, '/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> # pathlib.Path with a known ext (.mdf)
    >>> write_file(block, Path('/home/noise_param.mdf'))
    >>> # DataFile with a known ext (.pwdt)
    >>> write_file(group, DataFile('/home/noise_param.pwdt'))
    ```

    If the destination file `dst` has a missing or non-standard file
    extension, you can use the `dst_format` parameter. Alternatively,
    you can input an instance of
    `DataFile` as the `dst`
    argument and use the DataFile’s `format_override` parameter to
    define the destination’s format.

    ```
    >>> # no ext solved by dst_format
    >>> write_file(group, '/data/s_param', dst_format='mdif')
    >>> # non-standard ext solved by dst_format
    >>> write_file(block, '/data/noise_param.txt', dst_format='mdif')
    >>> # no ext solved by DataFile
    >>> write_file(group, DataFile('/data/noise_param', format_override='mdif'))
    ```

    If the destination file `dst` already exists, a FileExistsError is
    raised if `dst_mode='x'`, which is the default. A `dst_mode`
    parameter value of `'w'` will overwrite the entire existing file,
    while a value of `'a'` will append to the existing file.

    Note

    Only certain types of datafiles work for `dst_mode='a'`. A
    ValueError is raised if append mode is not supported for the format
    of `dst`.

    ```
    >>> # overwrite dst, if it exists
    >>> write_file(group, '/home/data/s_param.ds', dst_mode='w')
    >>> # append to dst, if it exists
    >>> write_file(block, '/home/data/noise_param.mdf', dst_mode='a')
    >>> # append to dst, if it exists
    >>> write_file(group, '/home/data/run1.pwdt', dst_mode='a')
    ```

    See also

    [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools._api.group.Group"), [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools._api.block.Block")


---

## 225. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.adsreadoptions}

# ADSReadOptions[](#adsreadoptions "Link to this heading")

*class* ADSReadOptions[](#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions "Link to this definition")
:   Options for ADS dataset reading.

    This object is immutable, so its properties cannot be changed after
    instantiation.

    Attributes

    |  |  |

    Parameters:

        used to read ADS datasets. If `None`, dsdump will be tried
        first. If there is no HPEESOF\_DIR environment variable set,
        then the `keysight-ads-dataset` module is used, Defaults
        to `None`.
