## 232. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.adswriteinvalid}

# ADSWriteInvalid[](#adswriteinvalid "Link to this heading")

*class* ADSWriteInvalid[](#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid "Link to this definition")
:   Options for writing invalid datapoints to ADS datasets.

    Each of the 5 generic datatypes has one or more available options for
    writing invalid data to ADS datasets. Additionally, there are options
    for NaN and null representations. NaN values only apply to floating
    and complexfloating datatypes. Note that the current implementation
    does not allow for separate definition of NaN for floating and
    complexfloating.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`boolean`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean") | Option for boolean data. |
    | [`boolean_options`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean_options.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean_options "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean_options") | All valid options for [`boolean`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.boolean") property. |
    | [`complexfloating`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.complexfloating.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.complexfloating "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.complexfloating") | Return option for complexfloating data. |
    | [`complexfloating_options`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.complexfloating_options.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.complexfloating_options "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.complexfloating_options") | Return all options for complexfloating data. |
    | [`floating`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.floating.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.floating "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.floating") | Return option for floating data. |
    | [`floating_options`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.floating_options.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.floating_options "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.floating_options") | Return all options for floating data. |
    | [`integer`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer") | Return option for integer data. |
    | [`integer_null_rep`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer_null_rep.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer_null_rep "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer_null_rep") | Return int that represents null values. |
    | [`integer_options`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer_options.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer_options "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.integer_options") | Return all options for integer data. |
    | [`nan_rep`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.nan_rep.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.nan_rep "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.nan_rep") | Return float that represents NaN values. |
    | [`read_or_write`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.read_or_write.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.read_or_write "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.read_or_write") | Return literal 'read' or 'write'. |
    | [`string`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string") | Return option for string data. |
    | [`string_null_rep`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string_null_rep.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string_null_rep "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string_null_rep") | Return str that represents null values. |
    | [`string_options`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string_options.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string_options "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.string_options") | Return all options for string data. |

ADSWriteInvalid.\_\_init\_\_(*boolean: Literal['float\_w\_nan', 'int\_w\_null'] = 'float\_w\_nan'*, *complexfloating: Literal['complex\_w\_nan'] = 'complex\_w\_nan'*, *floating: Literal['float\_w\_nan'] = 'float\_w\_nan'*, *integer: Literal['float\_w\_nan', 'int\_w\_null'] = 'float\_w\_nan'*, *string: Literal['str\_w\_null'] = 'str\_w\_null'*, *nan\_rep: float = nan*, *integer\_null\_rep: int = 99999*, *string\_null\_rep: str = 'null'*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSWriteInvalid.__init__ "Link to this definition")
:   Initialize instance of ADSWriteInvalid.

          datapoints.

          datapoints.
        * **floating** (*{“float\_w\_nan”}, default “float\_w\_nan”*) – Setting for writing float variables with invalid
          datapoints.

:   Initialize CITIReadOptions instance.

    Parameters:
    :   **engine\_pref** – If `"python"`, CITIfiles will be directly read using an
        engine written in Python. If `"ads"`, the CITIfile is
        converted to an intermediate ADS dataset, then the dataset is
        read using the `engine_pref` setting for ADS reading. If
        `None`, internal logic is used to determine which engine to
        use. Defaults to `None`.

## 273. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.CSVWriteOptions.__init__.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.csvwriteoptions.__init__}

# CSVWriteOptions.\_\_init\_\_[](#csvwriteoptions-init "Link to this heading")

CSVWriteOptions.\_\_init\_\_(*\**, *engine\_pref: Literal['pandas'] | None = None*, *pandas\_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None*, *cols\_default\_ints: Literal[1, 0] = 1*, *cols\_default\_ints\_forced: bool = False*, *cols\_dimscales\_delim: tuple[str, str, str] = ('[', ',', ']')*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.CSVWriteOptions.__init__ "Link to this definition")
:   Initialize CSVWriteOptions.

    Parameters:
    :   * **engine\_pref** (*{‘pandas’, None}, default None*) – Preference for writing CSV files. If `"pandas"`, use the
          pandas library. If None, use internal logic to determine the
          best engine.
        * **pandas\_kwargs** (*dict, optional*) – Keyword arguments to pass to the pandas writer. Only used if
          engine\_pref is `"pandas"`.
        * **cols\_default\_ints** (*{1, 0}, default 1*) – Only applies to multi-dimensional variables. The integer-based
          indexing to use for the columns in the event that any Var’s
          dimscales are not used. If `1`, use 1-based ints for
          the index labels. If `0`, use 0-based ints.
        * **cols\_default\_ints\_forced** (*bool, default False*) – Only applies to multi-dimensional variables. If `True`, use
          the integers set by cols\_default\_ints for the columns even if
          the Var has dimscales. If `False`, use the dimscales if they
          exist.
        * **cols\_dimscales\_delim, default (‘[’, ‘,’, ‘]’)** – Only applies to multi-dimensional variables. A 3-tuple of str
          characters used for embedding dimscales into the varnames in a
          flat string columns index. The first character is the opening
          delimiter, the second is the delimiter between dimscales, and
          the third is the closing delimiter. For example, the default
          delimiters would create varnames like `'S[2,1]'` and
          `'PortZ[1]'`.


---

## 277. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.datafile}

# DataFile[](#datafile "Link to this heading")

*class* DataFile[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "Link to this definition")
:   An object that represents a datafile on a filesystem.

    The datafile may or may not exist.

    Parameters:
    :   * **path\_or\_obj** – A str, path object, or file object that points to a file
          location. The file may or may not exist.
        * **format\_override** – Optionally override the format that would be inferred by the
          file extension. Also allows to assign a format to files with
          missing file extensions. If `None`, the format is
          determined by the file extension on `path_or_obj`. Defaults
          to `None`.

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following imports:

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import DataFile
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    ```

    You can create a DataFile by passing in a str path, a
    `pathlib.Path`, or another DataFile object.

    ```
    >>> # using a str path
    >>> datafile = DataFile('/home/s_param.s4p')
    >>> # using a pathlib.Path
    >>> datafile = DataFile(Path('/home/s_param.s4p'))
    >>> # using another DataFile
    >>> datafile2 = DataFile(datafile)
    ```

    If the file has a known file extension, the format is inferred
    automatically.

    ```
    >>> datafile = DataFile('/home/s_param.s4p')
    >>> datafile.get_format()
    'touchstone'
    ```

    If the file has a missing or unknown file extension, you can
    specify the `format_override` parameter.

    ```
    >>> datafile = DataFile('/home/noise.txt', format_override='mdif')
    >>> datafile.get_format()
    'mdif'
    ```

    Raises:
    :   * **ValueError** – If `path_or_obj` is a directory.
          If invalid `format_override` value.
        * **TypeError** – If `path_or_obj` is wrong type.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`ext`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.ext.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.ext "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.ext") | The file extension (an empty str if missing extension). |
    | [`folder`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.folder.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.folder "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.folder") | Full path to folder containing DataFile. |
    | [`format_override`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.format_override.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.format_override "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.format_override") | Optional str format which takes precedence over the file extension. |
    | [`name`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.name.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.name "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.name") | The file's stem plus extension, if present. |
    | [`path`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.path.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.path "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.path") | The full path to the file. |
    | [`stem`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.stem.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.stem "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.stem") | Base filename (filename without extension). |
    | [`suffix`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.suffix.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.suffix "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.suffix") | File extension (alias for ext property). |

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.__init__.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.__init__ "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.__init__")(path\_or\_obj[, format\_override]) | Initialize with a file path or object, and optional format override. |
    | [`copy`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.copy.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.copy "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.copy")(dst[, dst\_mode]) | Copy file to another location. |
    | [`delete`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.delete.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.delete "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.delete")([missing\_ok]) | Delete file on disk, if it exists. |
    | [`exists`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.exists.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.exists "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.exists")() | Return bool indicating if file exists. |
    | [`find_diffs`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.find_diffs.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.find_diffs "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.find_diffs")(other\_datafile) | Return list of diffs found comparing this file to another. |
    | [`get_format`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.get_format.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.get_format "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.get_format")() | Return format of file. |
    | [`has_format`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.has_format.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.has_format "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.has_format")(fmt) | Return boolean indicating whether instance has format provided. |
    | [`has_modtime_match`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.has_modtime_match.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.has_modtime_match "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.has_modtime_match")(otherfile) | Return bool indicating whether this file has same modtime as other. |
    | [`is_ads`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_ads.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_ads "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_ads")() | Return bool indicating whether file is an ADS dataset file. |
    | [`is_citi`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_citi.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_citi "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_citi")() | Return bool indicating whether file is a CITIFile. |
    | [`is_csv`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_csv.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_csv "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_csv")() | Return bool indicating whether file is a CSV file. |
    | [`is_farfieldio`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_farfieldio.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_farfieldio "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_farfieldio")() | Return bool indicating whether file is a FarfieldIO file. |
    | [`is_hfss_ffd`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_hfss_ffd.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_hfss_ffd "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_hfss_ffd")() | Return bool indicating whether file is an HFSS FFD file. |
    | [`is_loadpull`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_loadpull.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_loadpull "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_loadpull")() | Return bool indicating whether file is a loadpull file. |
    | [`is_mdif`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_mdif.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_mdif "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_mdif")() | Return bool indicating whether file is an MDIF file. |
    | [`is_mdm`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_mdm.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_mdm "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_mdm")() | Return bool indicating whether file is an MDM file. |
    | [`is_native`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_native.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_native "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_native")() | Return bool indicating whether file is a native pwdatatools file. |
    | [`is_s2pmdif`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_s2pmdif.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_s2pmdif "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.is_s2pmdif")() | Return bool indicating whether file is an S2PMDIF file. |

## 285. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.__init__.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.datafile.__init__}

# DataFile.\_\_init\_\_[](#datafile-init "Link to this heading")

DataFile.\_\_init\_\_(*path\_or\_obj: StrPathLike | BaseDataFile*, *format\_override: str | None = None*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.__init__ "Link to this definition")
:   Initialize with a file path or object, and optional format override.

    The file may or may not exist on the filesystem.

    Parameters:
    :   * **path\_or\_obj** – A str, path object, or file object that points to a file
          location. The file may or may not exist.
        * **format\_override** – Optionally override the format that would be inferred by the
          file extension. Also allows to assign a format to files with
          missing file extensions. If `None`, the format is
          determined by the file extension on `path_or_obj`. Defaults
          to `None`.

    Raises:
    :   * **ValueError** – If `path_or_obj` is a directory.
          If invalid `format_override` value.
        * **TypeError** – If `path_or_obj` is wrong type.

## 286. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.copy.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.datafile.copy}

# DataFile.copy[](#datafile-copy "Link to this heading")

DataFile.copy(*dst: StrPathLike | BaseDataFile*, *dst\_mode: Literal['x', 'w'] = 'x'*) → None[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.copy "Link to this definition")
:   Copy file to another location.

    Parameters:
    :   * **dst** – The destination as a str path, a `pathlib.Path`, or a
          `pwdatatools.BaseDataFile`.
        * **dst\_mode** – The mode to use when opening `dst`. If `dst` does not yet
          exist, both modes yield the same behavior. However, if
          attempting to copy to a pre-existing file, `'w'` overwrites
          the existing file, and `'x'` results in a FileExistsError.
          Defaults to `'x'`.

    Return type:
    :   *None*

    Raises:
    :   **ValueError** – If `dst_mode` is not `'x'` or `'w'`.
        If `dst_mode='x'` and `dst` already exists.


---

DataFile.find\_diffs(*other\_datafile: str | PathLike[str] | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools._api.datafile.DataFile")*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.find_diffs "Link to this definition")

## 310. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.read_as_block.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.datafile.read_as_block}

# DataFile.read\_as\_block[](#datafile-read-as-block "Link to this heading")

DataFile.read\_as\_block(*loc: str = '/'*, *\**, *data: bool = True*, *format\_specific: FormatSpecificReadOptions | None = None*, *idxs: IdxsOption | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*, *varnames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None*) → [Block](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.read_as_block "Link to this definition")
:   Read the DataFile and return a new instance of Block.

    If the DataFile has a missing or unknown file extension, you
    must specify the `Datafile.format_override` parameter. Known
    readable file extensions are stored in
    `options.reading.extensions`. Known readable file formats
    are stored in `options.reading.formats`.

    Parameters:
    :   * **loc** – The location within the DataFile to return as a Block. If
          `'/'` (the “root”), the entire DataFile is read. Otherwise,
          it represents some portion of the DataFile. This may be the
          name of a single datablock (for example, in an MDIF or ADS
          dataset), or the full HDF5 path to a block (an IvITrace) for
          a .pwdt file. Defaults to `'/'`.
        * **data** – A bool that determines whether to read the data. If `False`,
          only the metadata is read. Reading only metadata can be useful
          for quickly examining information about the variables. Defaults
          to `True`.
        * **format\_specific** – By default, the global option
          `options.reading.format_specific` sets all format-
          specific reading options, but this parameter can override the
          global options. If provided, it must be an instance of
          `FormatSpecificReadOptions`. See the docs for a list of
          all classes that can act as format-specific read options. Some
          examples are [`ADSReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions"),
          [`LoadPullReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions"), and [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars").
        * **idxs** (*{‘auto’, True, False}, optional*) – If `True`, create index variables (idxs) when reading the
          source file. If `False`, do not create them. If `'auto'`,
          use the format-specific defaults. If `None`, use the global
          option `options.reading.idxs`.
        * **iffs** – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing. Defaults to `False`.
        * **varnames** – A mapping of variable roles to their names. Defaults to
          `options.reading.varnames`.

    Return type:
    :   [*Block*](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")

    Raises:
    :   **ValueError** – If data cannot be represented as a single Block.

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following import:

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    ```

    If the DataFile has a known file extension, and you want to read
    the entire file, you can call `read_as_block` with any arguments.
    Known file extensions are stored in
    `options.reading.extensions`.

    ```
    >>> # Using a path with known ext (.lpd)
    >>> datafile = pwdt.DataFile('/home/device.lpd')
    >>> block = datafile.read_as_block()
    ```

    If the DataFile has a missing or unknown file extension, you must
    specify the DataFile’s `format_override` parameter.

    ```
    >>> datafile = pwdt.DataFile('/data/noise.txt', format_override='mdif')
    >>> block = datafile.read_as_block()
    ```

    If you want to perform a partial read, use the `loc` parameter.
    You have to know the name of the part that you want to read. A
    Block is always returned. If the contents of the part cannot be
    represented by a single Block, a ValueError is raised.

    ```
    >>> block = datafile.read_as_block(loc='/SP1.SP')
    ```

    See also

    `from_file()`, [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools._api.block.Block"), [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools._api.group.Group")


---

## 311. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.read_as_group.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.datafile.read_as_group}

# DataFile.read\_as\_group[](#datafile-read-as-group "Link to this heading")

DataFile.read\_as\_group(*loc: str = '/'*, *\**, *data: bool = True*, *format\_specific: FormatSpecificReadOptions | None = None*, *idxs: IdxsOption | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*, *varnames: Mapping[str, str] | None = None*) → [Group](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.read_as_group "Link to this definition")
:   Read the DataFile and return a new instance of Group.

    If the DataFile file has a missing or unknown file extension, you
    must specify the `DataFile.format_override`. Known readable file
    extensions are stored in `options.reading.extensions`. Known
    readable file formats are stored in
    `options.reading.formats`.

    Parameters:
    :   * **loc** – The location within the source file to return as a
          [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group"). If `'/'` (the “root”), the entire DataFile
          is read. Otherwise, it represents some portion of the file.
          This may be the name of a single datablock (for example in an
          MDIF or ADS dataset). Or, it may be the full HDF5 path in a
          .pwdt file. Defaults to `'/'`, which results in the full
          file contents returned as a [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group").
        * **dtypes** – Datatypes used for numpy ndarrays. Defaults to `None`, which
          results in automatic determination of the dtypes.
        * **data** – A bool that determines whether to read the data. If `False`,
          only the metadata is read. Reading only metadata can be useful
          for quickly examining the variable names and hierarchy.
          Defaults to `True`.
        * **format\_specific** – Defines the format-specific reading options. By default, the
          global option `options.reading.format_specific` sets
          all format-specific reading options, but this parameter can
          override the global options. If provided, it must be an
          instance of `FormatSpecificReadOptions`. See the docs
          for a list of all classes that can act as format-specific read
          options. Some examples are [`ADSReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.ADSReadOptions"),
          [`LoadPullReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions"), and [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars").
        * **idxs** (*{‘auto’, True, False}, optional*) – If `True`, create index variables (idxs) when reading the
          source file. If `False`, do not create them. If `'auto'`,
          use the format-specific defaults. If `None`, use the global
          option `options.reading.idxs`.
        * **iffs** – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing. Defaults to `False`.
        * **varnames** – A mapping of variable roles to their names. Defaults to
          `options.reading.varnames`.

    Return type:
    :   [*Group*](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools.Group")

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following import:

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    ```

    If the DataFile has a known file extension, and you want to read
    the entire file, you can simply call `read_as_group` without any
    arguments. Known file extensions are stored in
    `pwdatatools.options.reading.extensions`.

    ```
    >>> # Using a path with known ext (.ds)
    >>> datafile = pwdt.DataFile('/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> group = datafile.read_as_group()
    ```

    If the file has a missing or unknown file extension, specify the
    DataFile’s `format_override` parameter.

    ```
    >>> datafile = pwdt.DataFile('/noise.txt', format_override='mdif')
    >>> group = datafile.read_as_group()
    ```

    If you want to perform a partial read, use the `loc` parameter. You
    have to know the name of the part that you want to read from `src`.
    A Group will always be returned, even if the contents could be
    contained within a single Block (the Block is placed into a Group and
    the Group is returned).

    ```
    >>> # partial read of ADS dataset returns Group containing one Block
    >>> datafile = pwdt.DataFile('/home/s_param.ds')
    >>> group = datafile.read_as_group(loc='/SP1.SP')
    ```

    See also

    `from_file()`, [`Group`](keysight.pwdatatools.Group.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Group "keysight.pwdatatools._api.group.Group"), [`Block`](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools._api.block.Block")


---

## 312. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.read_as_loadpullblock.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.datafile.read_as_loadpullblock}

# DataFile.read\_as\_loadpullblock[](#datafile-read-as-loadpullblock "Link to this heading")

DataFile.read\_as\_loadpullblock(*\*\*kwargs*) → [LoadPullBlock](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools._api.loadpull.main.LoadPullBlock")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.read_as_loadpullblock "Link to this definition")
:   Read the DataFile and return a LoadPullBlock.

    The Datafile must have a known file extension that is associated
    with Keysight, Focus, or Maury load pull files. Known readable load
    pull file extensions are stored in
    `options.reading.format_to_extension_map['loadpull']`.

    Parameters:
    :   * **format\_specific** (*FormatSpecificReadOptions*) – Defines the format-specific reading options. By default, the
          global option `options.reading.format_specific.loadpull`
          sets format-specific loadpull reading options, but this
          parameter can override the global options. If provided, it
          must be an instance of `FormatSpecificReadOptions`. See
          the docs for a list of all classes that can act as format-
          specific read options. Some examples are
          [`LoadPullReadOptions`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions"), and [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars").
        * **varnames** (*Mapping[RoleLike, str]*) – A mapping of variable roles to their names. Defaults to
          `options.reading.varnames`.

    Return type:
    :   [*LoadPullBlock*](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")

    Examples

    Using all the default options:

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> datafile = pwdt.DataFile("/data/loadpull.cst")
    >>> lpblock = datafile.read_as_loadpullblock()
    ```

    Modifying global options to control how variables are named and
    which variables are derived from a and b waves:

    ```
    >>> pwdt.options.reading.varnames["power.delivered.load"] = "Pout"
    >>> pwdt.options.reading.format_specific.loadpull.derived_vars.ampm = False
    >>> lpblock = datafile.read_as_loadpullblock() # uses global options
    ```

    Passing in a dict of roles to varnames and an instance of
    [`LoadPullDerivedVars`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars") to override the global settings:

    ```
    >>> lpblock = datafile.read_as_loadpullblock(
    ...     "/data/loadpull.cst",
    ...     varnames={'gamma.load': 'GL'},
    ...     format_specific=pwdt.LoadPullDerivedVars(ampm=False),
    ... )
    ```

    Notes

    The indexing in the pandas DataFrame always uses `'ivars-idxs'`
    as the rows index and `'flat'` column index. The global
    indexing options are ignored.

    See also

    [`LoadPullBlock`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools._api.loadpull.main.LoadPullBlock"), [`LoadPullBlock.from_file()`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_file.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_file "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_file")


---

## 315. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.translate.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.datafile.translate}

# DataFile.translate[](#datafile-translate "Link to this heading")

DataFile.translate(*dst: str | PathLike[str] | [DataFile](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile "keysight.pwdatatools._api.datafile.DataFile")*, *dst\_mode: Literal['x', 'w', 'a'] = 'x'*, *\**, *dst\_format: str | None = None*, *iffs: bool = False*) → None[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.translate "Link to this definition")
:   Translate a DataFile to another file format.

    The destination format can be set explicitly using an optional
    keyword argument. However, if the `dst` has a recognized
    file extension, its format can be automatically inferred and
    the keyword argument isn’t needed.

    Parameters:
    :   * **dst** (*str, PathLike, or DataFile*) – The destination file path. If `dst_format=None`,
          attempts are made to ascertain the format by examining the
          destination file’s extension. Known file extensions are
          stored in `options.writing.extensions`.
        * **dst\_mode** (*{‘x’, ‘w’, ‘a’}, default ‘x’*) – The mode to use when opening `dst`. If `dst` does not yet
          exist, all three modes yield the same behavior. However, the 3
          modes have differing behaviors if attempting to write to a
          pre-existing file. `'w'` overwrites the existing file.
          `'a'` appends to the existing file. `'x'` results in a
          FileExistsError.
        * **dst\_format** (*str, optional*) – Sets the destination file’s format. Supported types are stored
          in `options.writing.formats`. Any value other than
          `None` overrides the format inferred from or set by `dst`.
        * **iffs** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, keep any intermediate files created during
          processing.

    Notes

    This method always uses the global format-specific read and
    write options. The only way to override the global options is to
    perform translation as a two-step process (read then write).

    Return type:
    :   *None*

    Examples

    The below examples assume the following imports:

    ```
    >>> from keysight.pwdatatools import DataFile
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    ```

    If the datafile’s [`get_format()`](keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.get_format.md#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.get_format "keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.get_format") is able to be determined and
    the destination file `dst` has a known file extension, simply
    input `dst` and nothing else.

    ```
    >>> src = DataFile('/home/s_param.s4p')
    >>> src.translate('/home/s_param.ds')  # known extensions (.s4p and .ds)
    >>> src.translate(Path('/home/noise.mdf')) # known extensions (.s4p and .mdf)
    ```

    If the the destination file `dst` has a missing or unknown file
    extension, use the `dst_format` parameter or a DataFile with
    `format_override` set.

    ```
    >>> src = DataFile('/home/s_param.s4p')
    >>> # using dst_format:
    >>> src.translate('/home/s_param', dst_format='mdif')
    >>> using a DataFile as dst:
    >>> dst = DataFile('/home/noise', format_override='mdif')
    >>> src.translate(dst)
    ```

    If the destination file `dst` already exists, a FileExistsError is
    raised if `dst_mode='x'`, which is the default. A `dst_mode`
    parameter value of `'w'` will overwrite the entire existing file,
    while a value of `'a'` will append to the existing file.

    Note

    Only certain types of datafiles work for `dst_mode='a'`. A
    ValueError is raised if append mode is not supported for the format
    of `dst`.

    ```
    >>> src = DataFile('/home/s_param.s4p')
    >>> src.translate('/s_param.ds', dst_mode='w')  # overwrite dst, if it exists
    >>> src.translate('/s_param.mdf', dst_mode='a') # append to dst, if it exists
    ```

    See also

    `translate_file()`, `read_file()`, `write_file()`


---

## 316. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.tree.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.datafile.tree}

# DataFile.tree[](#datafile-tree "Link to this heading")

DataFile.tree() → str[](#keysight.pwdatatools.DataFile.tree "Link to this definition")
:   Return a tree view of this DataFile, similar to a directory tree.

    In the tree, each Group is represented as a “folder” and each
    Block is represented as a “file”. The tree is returned as a string
    with newlines separating each level of the tree. The tree is
    indented to show the hierarchy. The string is meant to be printed
    to the console or shown in a GUI, not for programmatic use.

    Returns:
    :   Representation of the DataFile as a tree.

    Return type:
    :   *str*

    Notes

    This method scans the datafile to build the tree. Whenever possible,
    it does this without reading the data. The speed of the scan depends
    on the file format and the size of the file. For binary file formats,
    the scan can be very fast, even for large files. For text-based file
    formats, the scan can be slower.

    Examples

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> datafile = pwdt.DataFile('/home/s_param_and_HB.ds')
    >>> print(datafile.tree())
    <[/] Group 's_param_and_HB'>
    ├── <[0] Block 'Sweep2.Sweep1.SP1.SP' with 5 Vars>
    ├── <[1] Block 'HB1.HB' with 4 Vars>
    └── <[2] Block 'aele_0.HB1.HB' with 2 Vars>
    ```


---

## 323. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.__init__.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullreadoptions.__init__}

# LoadPullReadOptions.\_\_init\_\_[](#loadpullreadoptions-init "Link to this heading")

LoadPullReadOptions.\_\_init\_\_(*\**, *derived\_vars: [LoadPullDerivedVars](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "keysight.pwdatatools._file_io.reading.options_loadpull.LoadPullDerivedVars") | None = LoadPullDerivedVars(main=frozenset({'gain.transducer', 'power.delivered.load', 'gain.power', 'power.delivered.input', 'distortion.ampm', 'power.available.source', 'efficiency.drain', 'gamma.load', 'gamma.input', 'power.available.input', 'efficiency.power\_added'}), freq\_enums=frozenset({'gamma.load', 'gamma.input'}), power\_units='dBm')*, *always\_freq\_suffixed: Iterable[str] = {'gamma.input', 'gamma.load', 'gamma.source', 'impedance.input', 'impedance.load', 'impedance.source', 'wave.enumerated.incident', 'wave.enumerated.reflected'}*, *power\_ivar\_pref: Literal['power.available.input', 'power.available.source', None] = None*, *uniform\_ivars: bool = False*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullReadOptions.__init__ "Link to this definition")
:   Initialize instance.

    Parameters:
    :   * **derived\_vars** (*LoadPullDerivedVars, optional*) – Derived loadpull variables to include in data. If `None`,
          no derived variables will be calculated. Defaults to
          `LOADPULL_DERIVED_VARS_DEFAULT`.
        * **always\_freq\_suffixed** (*iterable of str, default {‘gamma.input’, ‘gamma.load’}*) – Roles that have an explicit fundamental frequency suffix in their
          variable names, even when it’s the only frequency component present.
          See notes for more information.
        * **power\_ivar\_pref** (*POWER\_IVAR\_PREF\_DEFAULT, optional*) – If `"power.available.input"`, the power ivar is set to the
          power available at the input. If `"power.delivered.input."`,
          the power ivar is set to the power delivered to the input of the
          device. If `"power.available.source"`, the power ivar is set to
          the power available at the source. If `None`, the
          `"power.available.input"` is preferred, followed by
          `"power.delivered.input"`, and finally `"power.available.source"`.
        * **uniform\_ivars** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, frequency and power ivars will be added, even if
          they are not swept in the datafile.

    Notes

    Regarding the fund\_freq\_suffix parameter:
    Many variables are assumed to be at the fundamental frequency, and therefore
    often have their frequency suffixes omitted. For example gain, efficiency,
    AMPM, etc. are all typically understood to be at the fundamental frequency. In
    cases where one of these variables only has a fundamental frequency component,
    the frequency suffix is left off, and it is instead implicitly understood to
    be at the fundamental. For example, “Gain\_F1” becomes “Gain”.

    This set includes the variables for which there should ALWAYS be a frequency
    suffix, even when there is only a fundamental frequency component. For example,
    use the variable names “GammaLoad\_F1” and “GammaIn\_F1” instead of “GammaLoad”
    and “GammaIn”.

## 326. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullderivedvars}

# LoadPullDerivedVars[](#loadpullderivedvars "Link to this heading")

*class* LoadPullDerivedVars[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars "Link to this definition")
:   Define loadpull variables to be calculated from A/B Waves.

    This object is immutable, so its properties cannot be changed after
    instantiation.

    Notes

    Some loadpull data file formats contain A/B wave data, which can be
    used to calculate additional “derived” loadpull variables. You can
    control which variables are derived by setting the [`main`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.main.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.main "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.main") and
    [`freq_enums`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.freq_enums.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.freq_enums "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.freq_enums") attributes.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`freq_enums`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.freq_enums.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.freq_enums "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.freq_enums") | Return the enumerated derived variables. |
    | [`main`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.main.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.main "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.main") | Return the main derived variables. |
    | [`power_units`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.power_units.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.power_units "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.power_units") | Return the power units. |
    | [`read_or_write`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.read_or_write.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.read_or_write "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.read_or_write") | Return literal 'read' or 'write'. |

    Methods

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`__init__`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.__init__.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.__init__ "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.__init__")(\*[, main, freq\_enums, power\_units]) | Initialize instance with optional kwargs. |
    | [`get_formats`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.get_formats.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.get_formats "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.get_formats")() | Return formats supported by this class. |
    | [`replace`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.replace.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.replace "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.replace")(\*\*kwargs) | Return a new instance with the specified properties replaced. |

## 331. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.__init__.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullderivedvars.__init__}

# LoadPullDerivedVars.\_\_init\_\_[](#loadpullderivedvars-init "Link to this heading")

LoadPullDerivedVars.\_\_init\_\_(*\**, *main: Iterable[str] = FrozenRolesSet(frozenset({'gain.transducer', 'power.delivered.load', 'gain.power', 'power.delivered.input', 'distortion.ampm', 'power.available.source', 'efficiency.drain', 'gamma.load', 'gamma.input', 'power.available.input', 'efficiency.power\_added'}))*, *freq\_enums: Iterable[str] = FrozenRolesSet(frozenset({'gamma.load', 'gamma.input'}))*, *power\_units: Literal['dBm', 'mW', 'W'] = 'dBm'*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullDerivedVars.__init__ "Link to this definition")
:   Initialize instance with optional kwargs.

    Enumerated frequencies are usually (but not necessarily)
    harmonically-related. There are options to individually control
    whether each derived variable is calculated at the enumerated
    frequencies.

    Parameters:
    :   * **main** (*iterable of str, default ALL\_DERIVED\_VARS\_ROLES*) – The derived variables that are calculated at the first
          enumerated frequency. Defaults to deriving all variables.
        * **freq\_enums** (*iterable of str, default DERIVED\_VARS\_FREQ\_ENUMS\_DEFAULT*) – The derived variables that are calculated at the enumerated
          frequencies. Defaults to deriving only the gamma.input and
          gamma.load variables.
        * **power\_units** (*{‘dBm’, ‘mW’, ‘W’}, default ‘dBm’*) – A string that determines the units of the power variables. Must
          be one of `"dBm"`, `"mW"`, or `"W"`.


---

*class* MDIFWriteInvalid[](#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid "Link to this definition")
:   Options for writing variables with invalid datapoints to MDIF.

    Each of the 5 generic datatypes has one or more available options for
    writing invalid data to MDIFs. Additionally, there are options for
    NaN and null representation in MDIF files. NaN values only apply to
    floating and complexfloating datatypes.

    Attributes

    |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [`boolean`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean") | Option for boolean data. |
    | [`boolean_options`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean_options.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean_options "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean_options") | All valid options for [`boolean`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.boolean") property. |
    | [`complexfloating`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.complexfloating.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.complexfloating "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.complexfloating") | Return option for complexfloating data. |
    | [`complexfloating_options`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.complexfloating_options.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.complexfloating_options "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.complexfloating_options") | Return all options for complexfloating data. |
    | [`floating`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.floating.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.floating "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.floating") | Return option for floating data. |
    | [`floating_options`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.floating_options.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.floating_options "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.floating_options") | Return all options for floating data. |
    | [`integer`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.integer.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.integer "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.integer") | Return option for integer data. |

    | [`string`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.string.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.string "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.string") | Return option for string data. |
    | [`string_null_rep`](keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.string_null_rep.md#keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.string_null_rep "keysight.pwdatatools.MDIFWriteInvalid.string_null_rep") | Return str that represents null values. |

:   Initialize TouchstoneReadOptions instance.

    Parameters:
    :   * **engine\_pref** (*{None, “python”, “rust”, “ads”}, default None*) – If `"rust"`, a Rust-based Touchstone parser is used. If
          `"python"`, a Python-based engine is used. If `"ads"`,
          the file is converted to an intermediate ADS dataset, then
          the dataset is read using the ``` engine_pref``setting for
          ADS reading. If ``None ```, internal logic is used to
          determine which engine to use (which usually picks “rust”).
        * **network\_blockname** (*str, default “Network”*) – Name of the network parameters block in the Touchstone file.

## 385. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock}

# LoadPullBlock[](#loadpullblock "Link to this heading")

*class* LoadPullBlock[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "Link to this definition")
:   A collection of Vars that represents load pull data.

    Load pull is a process by which the impedance presented to a device under
    test is systematically varied in order to assess its performance.

    Examples

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    ```

    Instantiate a LoadPullBlock with a gamma ivar, using the default
    naming pattern for the gamma idxname:

    ```
    >>> data = {
    ...     'GammaLoad': [0.5 + 0.4j, 0.4 + 0.1j, 0.3 + 0.2j],
    ...     'iGammaLoad': [0, 1, 2],
    ...     'Gain': [10, 11, 12]
    ... }
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(data, gamma_ivarname='GammaLoad')
    >>> lpblock.gamma_ivarname
    'GammaLoad'
    >>> lpblock.gamma_idxname
    'iGammaLoad'
    ```

    Since the default naming pattern was used for gamma\_idxname, we
    did not have to specify it during initialization.

    Instantiate a LoadPullBlock with a gamma ivar and a power ivar. Note
    that when gamma and power are swept, the power sweep is always the
    inner sweep.

    ```
    >>> data = {
    ...     'GammaLoad': [0.5 + 0.4j, 0.5 + 0.4j, 0.4 + 0.1j, 0.4 + 0.1j],
    ...     'iGammaLoad': [0, 0, 1, 1],
    ...     'PSource': [-10.0, -8.0, -10.0, -8.0],
    ...     'iPSource': [0, 1, 0, 1],
    ...     'Gain': [10, 11, 12, 10.5, 11.5]
    ... }
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(
    ...     data,
    ...     gamma_ivarname='GammaLoad',
    ...     power_ivarname='PSource',
    ... )
    >>> lpblock.gamma_ivarname
    'GammaLoad'
    >>> lpblock.gamma_idxname
    'iGammaLoad'
    >>> lpblock.power_ivarname
    'PSource'
    >>> lpblock.power_idxname
    'iPSource'
    ```

    Since we did not specify the power\_idxname, it was assumed to be
    “iPSource”, which is the default naming pattern (“i” + “PSource”).

    See also

    The `read_file_as_loadpullblock()`
    function is the easiest way to instantiate a LoadPullBlock from a
    file. For more detailed information and examples, see
    [Work with Load Pull Data](../../howto/work_with_loadpull_data.md#work-with-load-pull-data).

## 401. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.__init__.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.__init__}

# LoadPullBlock.\_\_init\_\_[](#loadpullblock-init "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.\_\_init\_\_(*variables: Variables = None*, *\**, *name: str | None = None*, *gamma\_ivarname: str | None = None*, *gamma\_idxname: str | None = None*, *z\_ivarname: str | None = None*, *z\_idxname: str | None = None*, *power\_ivarname: str | None = None*, *power\_idxname: str | None = None*, *outer\_ivarnames: Iterable[str] | None = None*, *outer\_idxnames: Iterable[str | None] | None = None*, *exprs: ExprsDictLike | None = None*, *attrs: AttrsDictLike | None = None*, *copy: bool = False*, *\*\*kwargs*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.__init__ "Link to this definition")
:   Initialize an instance of LoadPullBlock.

    Parameters:
    :   * **variables** (*DataFrame, sequence of Var, str to VarLike mapping, or None*) – Several types of inputs are supported: a pandas DataFrame, a
          mapping of str variable name to ArrayLikes or Vars, or a sequence
          of Vars. Examples of ArrayLike objects are numpy ndarrays and
          MaskedArrays, Python lists, and pandas Series. If a mapping or
          sequence is provided, all data objects must have the same length
          for axis 0.
        * **name** (*str, optional*) – A str name for the LoadPullBlock. If not specified, the name is
          set to an empty string.
        * **gamma\_ivarname** (*str, optional*) – The name of the gamma independent variable. A LoadPullBlock
          must have either a gamma ivar or a z ivar, but not both.
        * **gamma\_idxname** (*str, optional*) – The name of the gamma indepedent variable’s index.
        * **z\_ivarname** (*str, optional*) – The name of the impedance independent variable. A LoadPullBlock
          must have either a gamma ivar or a z ivar, but not both.
        * **z\_idxname** (*str, optional*) – The name of the impedance indepedent variable’s index.
        * **power\_ivarname** (*str, optional*) – The name of the power independent variable.
        * **power\_idxname** (*str, optional*) – The name of the power indepedent variable’s index.
        * **outer\_ivarnames** (*iterable of str, optional*) – The names of the outer independent variables. Outer ivars can be
          any arbitrary swept variables, such as frequency, bias, etc.
        * **outer\_idxnames** (*iterable of str | None, optional*) – The names of the outer indepedent variable’s indexes.
        * **exprs** (*ExprsDictLike, optional*) – A mapping of str expression name to Expr objects. The Expr objects
          represent expressions that can be applied to variables or other
          expressions.
        * **attrs** (*dict-like, optional*) – A dict or dict-like object of arbitrary Block-level metadata. The
          keys must be strings and the values must be one of the following:
          str, int, float, complex, bool, None, dict, list, or
          numpy.ndarray. Nested dicts and lists are allowed.
        * **copy** (*bool, default False*) – If True, make a copy of the input variables. If False, use the
          input variables as-is, if possible.

    Other Parameters:
    :   * **data** (*DataFrame, str to ArrayLike mapping, or None*) – A keyword-only argument that exists mostly for backwards
          compatibility. It is recommended to use variables instead of this
          keyword-only argument. You cannot specify values for both data
          and variables.
        * **idxnames** (*iterable of str | None, optional*) – Optional iterable of names for variables that will be converted
          into indexes (idxs) for the ivars. If any of the ivars do not have
          an associated idx, the corresponding idxname should be None. This
          is another way to define the names of the gamma, z, power, and
          outer indexes. To use this argument, you must also specify
          ivarnames and variables input must contain Vars with the
          proper gamma/z/power roles. Defaults to `None`.
        * **ivarnames** (*iterable of str, optional*) – The names of the independent variables. This is another way
          to define the names of the gamma, z, power, and outer
          independent variables. To use this argument, variables
          input must contain Vars with the proper gamma/z/power roles.
          Defaults to `None`.

    Notes

    If an ivarname is provided and its associated idxname is not
    provided, then its idxname is assumed to be “i” + “ivarname”.
    For example, if gamma\_ivarname is “GammaLoad” and gamma\_idxname
    is not provided, then gamma\_idxname is assumed to be “iGammaLoad”.

    Examples

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    ```

    Instantiate a LoadPullBlock with a gamma ivar, using the default
    naming pattern for the gamma idxname:

    ```
    >>> data = {
    ...     'GammaLoad': [0.5 + 0.4j, 0.4 + 0.1j, 0.3 + 0.2j],
    ...     'iGammaLoad': [0, 1, 2],
    ...     'Gain': [10, 11, 12]
    ... }
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(data, gamma_ivarname='GammaLoad')
    >>> lpblock.gamma_ivarname
    'GammaLoad'
    >>> lpblock.gamma_idxname
    'iGammaLoad'
    ```

    Since the default naming pattern was used for gamma\_idxname, we
    did not have to specify it during initialization.

    Instantiate a LoadPullBlock with a gamma ivar and a power ivar. Note
    that when gamma and power are swept, the power sweep is always the
    inner sweep.

    ```
    >>> data = {
    ...     'GammaLoad': [0.5 + 0.4j, 0.5 + 0.4j, 0.4 + 0.1j, 0.4 + 0.1j],
    ...     'iGammaLoad': [0, 0, 1, 1],
    ...     'PSource': [-10.0, -8.0, -10.0, -8.0],
    ...     'iPSource': [0, 1, 0, 1],
    ...     'Gain': [10, 11, 12, 10.5, 11.5]
    ... }
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(
    ...     data,
    ...     gamma_ivarname='GammaLoad',
    ...     power_ivarname='PSource',
    ... )
    >>> lpblock.gamma_ivarname
    'GammaLoad'
    >>> lpblock.gamma_idxname
    'iGammaLoad'
    >>> lpblock.power_ivarname
    'PSource'
    >>> lpblock.power_idxname
    'iPSource'
    ```

    Since we did not specify the power\_idxname, it was assumed to be
    “iPSource”, which is the default naming pattern (“i” + “PSource”).

    See also

    The `read_file_as_loadpullblock()`
    function is the easiest way to instantiate a LoadPullBlock from a
    file. For more detailed information and examples, see
    [Work with Load Pull Data](../../howto/work_with_loadpull_data.md#work-with-load-pull-data).


---

## 402. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_gcomp.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.at_gcomp}

# LoadPullBlock.at\_gcomp[](#loadpullblock-at-gcomp "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.at\_gcomp(*gcomp\_values: float | int | ArrayLike*, *gain\_varname: str*, *\**, *gcomp\_varname: str = 'auto'*, *extrap: bool = False*) → [LoadPullBlock](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_gcomp "Link to this definition")
:   Return a new LoadPullBlock at specified gain compression value(s).

    Interpolation and/or extrapolation is performed if needed.

    Parameters:
    :   * **gcomp\_values** – Gain compression values at which to calculate all responses.
          Can be a single float value, a list of values, or a numpy
          array.
        * **gain\_varname** – The name of the gain variable to use to calculate compression.
        * **gcomp\_varname, default ‘auto’** – The name of the new calculated gain compression variable.
          Defaults to `'auto'`, which results in a varname of
          `'gain_varname' + '_comp'`.
        * **extrap, default False** – If `True`, extrapolate the data (if needed). If `False`,
          points requested that are outside of the available the data
          regions will be filled with NaN values.

    Return type:
    :   [*LoadPullBlock*](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")

    Examples

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(...)  # start with a LoadPullBlock
    >>> # Calculate the data at 0.5dB Gain compression point
    >>> lpblock_at_gcomp = lpblock.at_gcomp(0.5, 'Gain')
    ```


---

## 403. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_power.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.at_power}

# LoadPullBlock.at\_power[](#loadpullblock-at-power "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.at\_power(*power\_values: float | int | ArrayLike*, *power\_varname: str*, *\**, *interp: bool = True*, *extrap: bool = False*, *interp\_method: Literal['cubic', 'linear'] = 'cubic'*, *extrap\_method: Literal['cubic', 'linear', 'constant'] = 'cubic'*) → [LoadPullBlock](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_power "Link to this definition")
:   Return a new LoadPullBlock at specified power value(s).

    Parameters:
    :   * **power\_values** – Power value(s) at which to calculate all responses.
        * **power\_varname** – The name of the power variable to use for calculations.
        * **interp, default True** – If `True`, interpolate the data (if needed). If `False`,
          points requested that fall between existing data points are
          filled with NaNs.
        * **extrap, default False** – If `True`, extrapolate the data (if needed). If `False`,
          points requested that are outside of the available the data
          regions are filled with NaN values.
        * **interp\_method, default ‘cubic’** – The interpolation method to use.
        * **extrap\_method, default ‘cubic’** – The extrapolation method to use.

    Return type:
    :   [*LoadPullBlock*](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")

    Notes

    If `interp=False` and `extrap_method='cubic'`, interpolation
    is performed as a side effect of extrapolation.

    Examples

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(...)  # start with a LoadPullBlock
    >>> # Calculate the data at 42 dBm PLoad
    >>> lpblock_at_power = lpblock.at_power(42.0, 'PLoad')
    ```


---

## 405. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.contourplot.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.contourplot}

# LoadPullBlock.contourplot[](#loadpullblock-contourplot "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.contourplot(*z: str*, *\**, *ax=None*, *sca: bool = False*, *levels: int | ArrayLike | None = None*, *add\_xlabel: bool = True*, *add\_ylabel: bool = True*, *xlabel: str | None = None*, *ylabel: str | None = None*, *\*\*kwargs*)[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.contourplot "Link to this definition")
:   Plot contour lines on a matplotlib Axes.

    A matplotlib QuadContourSet object is returned, which can be used
    to further customize the plot. If you need access to the
    underlying Axes object, use the QuadContourSet’s `axes`
    attribute.

    LoadPullBlocks with a power ivar or outer ivars are not supported.
    If you want to plot contours for a LoadPullBlock with a power
    ivar, you must first get rid of the power dependnecy by selecting
    a subset of the data. There are several ways of doing this,
    including `LoadPullBlock.loc` and the following
    LoadPullBlock methods: [`at_power()`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_power.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_power "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_power"), [`at_gcomp()`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_gcomp.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_gcomp "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.at_gcomp"), and
    `xs()`.

    The same limitation is true of LoadPullBlocks with outer ivar(s),
    such as frequency, bias, etc. You must select a subset of the
    data before plotting.

    Parameters:
    :   * **z** – Name of the z variable to plot. The x and y variables are
          always the real and imaginary parts of the gamma ivar.
        * **ax** – An optional matplotlib Axes object. If `None`, use the
          current matplotlib Axes. Defaults to `None`.
        * **sca** – A bool that determines whether to set the Axes used for
          plotting as the current Axes. Invokes
          `matplotlib.pyplot.sca()`. Defaults to `False`.
        * **levels** (*int or array-like, optional*) – Determines the number and positions of the contour lines or
          regions. If an int, use matplotlib’s MaxNLocator, which tries
          to automatically choose no more than n+1 “nice” contour levels
          between minimum and maximum numeric values of Z. If array-
          like, draw contour lines at the specified levels. The values
          must be in increasing order.
        * **add\_xlabel** – If `True`, add an x label to the Axes. Defaults to `True`.
        * **add\_ylabel** – If `True`, add a y label to the Axes. Defaults to `True`.
        * **xlabel** – If `add_xlabel` is `True`, use this as the x label. If
          `None`, auto-create the label. Auto-creation tries to use
          the name of the x variable. If name of the variable is
          unknown, use the default of label, which is `'x'`. Defaults
          to `None`.
        * **ylabel** – If `add_ylabel` is `True`, use this as the y label. If
          `None`, auto-create the label. Auto-creation tries to use
          the name of the y variable. If name of the variable is
          unknown, use the default of label, which is `'y'`. Defaults
          to `None`.
        * **\*\*kwargs** – Additional keyword arguments are passed on to
          `matplotlib.pyplot.contour`.

    Returns:
    :   A matplotlib QuadContourSet instance.

    Return type:
    :   QuadContourSet

    Raises:
    :   **ValueError** – If there is no gamma or impedance ivar.
        If there is a power ivar or any outer ivars.

    Examples

    Start with a LoadPullBlock:
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(…)

    Plot Gain contours on a rectangular chart:
    >>> lpblock.contourplot(‘Gain’)

    Plot Gain contours on a Smith chart:
    >>> contourset = lpblock.contourplot(‘Gain’)
    >>> from kesight.pwdatatools import viz
    >>> viz.draw\_smith\_chart(contourset.axes)

    Plot red DrainEff contours on the same Axes as Gain contours:
    >>> lpblock.contourplot(‘DrainEff’, ax=contourset.axes, colors=’red’)

    Return the QuadContourSet object, and use it to further customize:
    >>> cs = lpblock.contourplot(‘Gain’)
    >>> plt.clabel(cs, inline=True, fontsize=9, fmt=’%.1f’)


---

## 406. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.coord_system.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.coord_system}

# LoadPullBlock.coord\_system[](#loadpullblock-coord-system "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.coord\_system() → Literal['rect', 'polar'] | None[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.coord_system "Link to this definition")
:   If data is gridded, return the grid’s coordinate system (‘rect’ or ‘polar’).

    If data is not gridded, return `None`.

    To be considered “gridded”, the following conditions must be met:
    1) The data must have either a gamma or impedance dependency.
    2) The gamma or impedance values must be regularly-spaced.
    3) There must be the same number of y points for each x point.
    4) If the data also has a power-depedency (in addition to gamma or
    impedance), the 2D grid must be identical for each power value.

    If the data does not meet the specified conditions, it is not
    considered “gridded”, and `None` is returned.

    If the data has a frequency dependency, the 2D grid can have
    different spacing, number of points, and extents at each frequency
    point, but the coordinate system (‘rect’ or ‘polar’) must be
    consistent (a ValueError is raised if not). If, at any frequency,
    the data does not meet the conditions to be considered “gridded”,
    `None` is returned.

    Return type:
    :   {‘rect’, ’polar’, None}

    Examples

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(...)  # start with a LoadPullBlock
    >>> # Determine the coordinate system of the data
    >>> coord_system = lpblock.coord_system()
    >>> if coord_system is None:
    ...     print('Data is not gridded.')
    >>> elif coord_system == 'rect':
    ...     print('Data is gridded in rectangular coordinates.')
    >>> elif coord_system == 'polar':
    ...     print('Data is gridded in polar coordinates.')
    ```


---

## 407. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.copy.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.copy}

# LoadPullBlock.copy[](#loadpullblock-copy "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.copy() → Self[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.copy "Link to this definition")
:   Return a deep copy of self.

    Notes

    The underlying data in each Var does not need to be copied; only
    metadata needs to be copied. Therefore, this is relatively inexpensive.

## 410. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.drop_grid_edges.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.drop_grid_edges}

# LoadPullBlock.drop\_grid\_edges[](#loadpullblock-drop-grid-edges "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.drop\_grid\_edges(*depth: int = 1*, *circular: bool | Literal['auto'] = 'auto'*) → [LoadPullBlock](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools._api.loadpull.main.LoadPullBlock")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.drop_grid_edges "Link to this definition")
:   Return new LoadPullBlock with grid pts along outer edges removed.

    Parameters:
    :   * **depth** – The number of “rows” of outer grid points to remove from each
          edge of the grid. For example, if depth=1, the outermost grid
          points are removed. If depth=2, the outermost 2 rows of grid
          points are removed along each edge.
        * **circular** – Either a bool or `'auto'`. Only applies for grids with
          a polar coordinate system and if drop\_edges is `True`. If
          `'auto'`, automatically determine if the grid is circular or
          donut shaped and if so, only drop grid points around the
          circumference. Otherwise, if a bool, respect the parameter
          setting. Defaults to `'auto'`.

    Return type:
    :   [*LoadPullBlock*](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")

    Examples

    ```
    >>> from keysight import pwdatatools as pwdt
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock(...)  # start with a LoadPullBlock
    >>> # The LoadPullBlock must be gridded
    >>> lpblock_gridded = lpblock.grid_data('rect', drop_edges=False)
    >>> # Remove the outermost 2 rows of grid points along each edge
    >>> lpblock_no_edges = lpblock_gridded.drop_grid_edges(depth=2)
    ```


---

## 411. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.drop_invalid_regular.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.drop_invalid_regular}

# LoadPullBlock.drop\_invalid\_regular[](#loadpullblock-drop-invalid-regular "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.drop\_invalid\_regular() → [LoadPullBlock](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools._api.loadpull.main.LoadPullBlock")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.drop_invalid_regular "Link to this definition")
:   Return a new LoadPullBlock with all NaN and null values removed.

    The observations are dropped in such a way as to maintain
    regularity of the power sweeps at each Gamma or Impedance value.
    If there are outer ivars, power sweeps are NOT regularized across
    outer ivar values.

    If there is no power sweep, the NaN and null values are simply dropped.

    Return type:
    :   [*LoadPullBlock*](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")


---

## 412. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.drop_observations.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.drop_observations}

# LoadPullBlock.drop\_observations[](#loadpullblock-drop-observations "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.drop\_observations(*condition: BoolArrayLike1D*) → Self[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.drop_observations "Link to this definition")
:   Return a new filtered Block without the specified observations.

    Parameters:
    :   **condition** (*1D bool array-like*) – A 1D boolean array-like with the same length as the Block’s
        axis 0, with True values at the indexes of the observations
        to drop.

    Returns:
    :   A new Block with the observations dropped where condition
        is True.

    Return type:
    :   [*Block*](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")

    Examples

    ```
    >>> block = pwdt.Block(data={'Vout': [1, 2, 3], 'Vin': [4, 5, 6]})
    >>> vout = block['Vout']
    >>> vin = block['Vin']
    >>> block.drop_observations(vout > 2)
    <Block with 2 variables and 1 observation>
    >>> block.drop_observations((vout == 1) & (vin >= 4))
    <Block with 2 variables and 1 observation>
    >>> block.drop_observations(vout == 1 | vin >= 4)
    <Block with 2 variables and 1 observation>
    ```


---

# LoadPullBlock.drop\_vars\_in\_place[](#loadpullblock-drop-vars-in-place "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.drop\_vars\_in\_place(*varnames: Iterable[str]*) → None[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.drop_vars_in_place "Link to this definition")

## 415. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.eval_expr_as_var.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.eval_expr_as_var}

# LoadPullBlock.eval\_expr\_as\_var[](#loadpullblock-eval-expr-as-var "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.eval\_expr\_as\_var(*key: str*) → [Var](keysight.pwdatatools.Var.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Var "keysight.pwdatatools._core.variables.var.Var")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.eval_expr_as_var "Link to this definition")
:   Evaluate the expression and return the result as a Var.

    Parameters:
    :   **key** (*str*) – The name of the expression to evaluate. It must exist in the
        Block’s [`exprs`](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.exprs.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.exprs "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.exprs") attribute.

    Notes

    The returned Var is not automatically added to the Block. If you
    want to add the Var to the Block, add it like this:

    ```
    >>> block["x"] = block.eval_expr_as_var("x")
    ```

    But note that not all expressions can be added as a Var to the Block.
    Only expressions that evaluate to the same length as the Block’s
    observations can be added as a Var.


---

## 416. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.fill_nan.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.fill_nan}

# LoadPullBlock.fill\_nan[](#loadpullblock-fill-nan "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.fill\_nan(*value: FloatNumber*, *\**, *in\_place: bool = False*) → Self[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.fill_nan "Link to this definition")
:   FIll all NaN values in all Vars and return a new Block or a reference to this Block.

    Parameters:
    :   * **value** (*float | int | np.floating | np.integer*) – The value to use for filling NaN values.
        * **in\_place** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, fill NaN values in place and return a reference to this Block.
          If `False`, return a new Block with NaN values filled.

    Return type:
    :   [*Block*](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")

    Notes

    Unlike [`Var.fill_nan()`](keysight.pwdatatools.Var.fill_nan.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Var.fill_nan "keysight.pwdatatools.Var.fill_nan"), this method does not allow for a
    complex fill value, since that doesn’t work for float variables.


---

## 417. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.fill_null.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.fill_null}

# LoadPullBlock.fill\_null[](#loadpullblock-fill-null "Link to this heading")

LoadPullBlock.fill\_null(*values: [FillValues](keysight.pwdatatools.FillValues.md#keysight.pwdatatools.FillValues "keysight.pwdatatools.FillValues") | None = None*, *\**, *in\_place: bool = False*) → Self[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.fill_null "Link to this definition")
:   Fill all null values in all Vars and return a new Block or a reference to this Block.

    Parameters:
    :   * **values** (*FillValues, optional*) – An optional instance of [`FillValues`](keysight.pwdatatools.FillValues.md#keysight.pwdatatools.FillValues "keysight.pwdatatools.FillValues"). If not provided,
          the default fill values are used.
        * **in\_place** (*bool, default False*) – If `True`, fill null values in place and return a reference to this Block.
          If `False`, return a new Block with null values filled.

    Return type:
    :   [*Block*](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools.Block")

    Notes

    Here are the default fill values for each dtype:

    * float: NaN
    * complex: NaN + 1j \* NaN
    * integer: 0
    * boolean: False
    * string: ‘’


---

## 418. api_reference\_autosummary\keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_block.md {#api_reference--_autosummary--keysight.pwdatatools.loadpullblock.from_block}

# LoadPullBlock.from\_block[](#loadpullblock-from-block "Link to this heading")

*classmethod* LoadPullBlock.from\_block(*block: [Block](keysight.pwdatatools.Block.md#keysight.pwdatatools.Block "keysight.pwdatatools._api.block.Block")*) → [LoadPullBlock](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools._api.loadpull.main.LoadPullBlock")[](#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.from_block "Link to this definition")

    Return type:
    :   [*LoadPullBlock*](keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock.md#keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock "keysight.pwdatatools.LoadPullBlock")

    Examples

    >>> block = pwdt.Block.from_file("/data/loadpull.cst")
    >>> lpblock = pwdt.LoadPullBlock.from_block(block)
    ```
